## Overview

Package telatest tests Tela UIs without a window: it mounts a tree in a headless window, simulates a user with real pointer and key events, finds elements by role and text like Playwright, and compares the pixels with goldens (ARCHITECTURE section 17).

```go
func TestCounter(t *testing.T) {
    app := telatest.Mount(t, Counter(), telatest.Size(400, 300))
    app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment"))
    app.ExpectText("Count: 1")
    app.Golden("counter.png") // testdata/counter.png; TELA_UPDATE=1 regenerates
}
```

### Locators

[`ByRole`](#func-byrole), [`ByText`](#func-bytext) and [`ByClass`](#func-byclass) describe an element by what a user (or an assistive technology) sees, resolved against the semantics tree each time they are used; [`ByTestID`](#func-bytestid) finds the element that carries an h.TestID, for those a user cannot name (like data-testid, it is not in the aria snapshot). A locator that matches none or several elements makes an action fail with the aria snapshot and the closest names; narrow it with [`Locator.Filter`](#func-locator-filter) and [`Locator.Nth`](#func-locator-nth). Hidden elements are never matched.

### Actions and auto-wait

[`App.Click`](#func-app-click) (with [`Right`](#func-right) for the secondary button and [`Delay`](#func-delay) for a held one), [`App.DoubleClick`](#func-app-doubleclick), [`App.Tap`](#func-app-tap), [`App.LongPress`](#func-app-longpress), [`App.Hover`](#func-app-hover), [`App.Focus`](#func-app-focus), [`App.Scroll`](#func-app-scroll), [`App.Drag`](#func-app-drag), [`App.DragBy`](#func-app-dragby), [`App.Press`](#func-app-press), [`App.Type`](#func-app-type) and [`App.Fill`](#func-app-fill) act like a user. The pointer actions move the pointer to the element's center and send pointer events through hit-testing and the gesture arena (hover and :active states, focus on press, click counts, drags); Tap and LongPress use a touch pointer. The keyboard actions send key events to the focused element (typing into a focused text field; Fill replaces a field's value like Playwright's fill).

Before acting, an action waits until the element is visible, enabled, in view and not covered by another element. Before and after, the app is settled: pending state updates are applied and frames run, advancing the app's clock to each one, until nothing is dirty and no animation or scroll fling is running: transitions (hover:, focus:, dark: changes with transition classes) and finite animations run to their end, so a screenshot after an action shows the settled state. Infinite animations (animate-spin, animate-pulse) are never waited for, and use [`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance) to step them. An app that never goes quiet otherwise (a goroutine that updates state all the time) is not waited for either: the first time it is logged, and actions then run only a few frames. Both are decided in app time ([`Timeout`](#func-timeout) of it), so a slow machine never cuts a finite animation short.

[`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance) moves the clock by hand: it is how a test waits for a long-press timer, an animation or a fade. To capture the frames of an animation, mount with [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle): actions, screenshots and the queries ([`App.AriaSnapshot`](#func-app-ariasnapshot), [`App.Count`](#func-app-count), [`App.Bounds`](#func-app-bounds), [`App.Stats`](#func-app-stats), [`App.Cursor`](#func-app-cursor)) then leave running animations where they are, and only Advance moves them (ADR-097).

The expectations ([`App.ExpectText`](#func-app-expecttext), [`App.ExpectNoText`](#func-app-expectnotext), [`App.ExpectRole`](#func-app-expectrole), [`App.ExpectCount`](#func-app-expectcount), [`App.ExpectFocused`](#func-app-expectfocused), [`App.ExpectValue`](#func-app-expectvalue), [`App.ExpectAria`](#func-app-expectaria) and [`App.Expect`](#func-app-expect)) retry until they hold or the [`Timeout`](#func-timeout) expires, letting a frame of app time and a moment of real time pass between tries, so state set by a goroutine arrives (under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle) the first try does not move the clock: it handles only the work due). [`App.Expect`](#func-app-expect) checks the states of an element ([`Checked`](#func-checked), [`Disabled`](#func-disabled), [`Expanded`](#func-expanded), [`Selected`](#func-selected), [`Pressed`](#func-pressed), [`Focused`](#func-focused), [`HasName`](#func-hasname), [`HasValue`](#func-hasvalue)) without matching strings of the aria snapshot.

[`App.ClickAt`](#func-app-clickat) and [`App.DragFromTo`](#func-app-dragfromto) act at window coordinates, for what a locator cannot name; [`App.Bounds`](#func-app-bounds) returns an element's box as a tela.Rect. [`App.PixelAt`](#func-app-pixelat) reads the frame, [`App.Measure`](#func-app-measure) returns the work the tree did during some actions, and [`MountFunc`](#func-mountfunc) is Mount for one component. [`MountApp`](#func-mountapp) mounts a tela.App's Root in the app's own window (its size, root class, color scheme, theme and class aliases, and the fields of the OS window: Title, size limits, Frameless, Hidden, Placement, OnClose...), the App that tela.Main runs and `tela snapshot` reads from the package; [`FromApp`](#func-fromapp) gives the settings that shape what is drawn to Mount, Render and the other entry points.

### Windows

An app has one window per tela.Window that is mounted, besides its main window. The headless backend plays a fake window manager (ADR-179): it grants every request at once, gives hidden and minimized windows no frames, and records parents, modality, hit regions and caption presses. The app still builds and runs the effects of a hidden or minimized window, as on a desktop (ADR-185): a tray item clicked while the main window is hidden updates its state, its tray menu and the windows it opens; settling waits for that work, and the window draws it when shown.

An [`App`](#type-app) is scoped to one window. Mount returns the one of the main window; [`App.Windows`](#func-app-windows) lists the open windows (in the order they opened, the main window first), [`App.Window`](#func-app-window) selects one by title, [`App.WindowAt`](#func-app-windowat) by index and [`App.LastWindow`](#func-app-lastwindow) is the newest, and [`App.WaitForWindow`](#func-app-waitforwindow) runs a step and returns the window it opened, like Playwright's context.pages() and page.waitForEvent('popup'). Each returns an App with the same queries, actions, expectations, goldens and pixels as the main one, working on that window: it is always the same App for the same window.

```go
settings := app.WaitForWindow(func() {
    app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Settings"))
})
settings.ExpectText("Preferences")
settings.Golden("settings.png")
```

Selecting a window waits for it to open, like a locator waits for its element; the clock, settling and the end of the app belong to the whole app, so an action in one window waits for the work it causes in the others. A pointer press or a key in a window that is not the active one activates it first, as the user clicking or typing there does.

The window itself: [`App.Title`](#func-app-title), [`App.WindowState`](#func-app-windowstate) (tela.WindowState, as UseWindow sees it), [`App.WindowSize`](#func-app-windowsize), [`App.Placement`](#func-app-placement), [`App.Modal`](#func-app-modal), [`App.Parent`](#func-app-parent), [`App.Blocks`](#func-app-blocks), [`App.BlockedBy`](#func-app-blockedby) and [`App.Closed`](#func-app-closed); the expectations [`App.ExpectTitle`](#func-app-expecttitle), [`App.ExpectWindowState`](#func-app-expectwindowstate) (with [`Maximized`](#func-maximized), [`Fullscreen`](#func-fullscreen), [`Minimized`](#func-minimized), [`Hidden`](#func-hidden), [`Active`](#func-active) and [`ClientDecorations`](#func-clientdecorations)), [`App.ExpectClosed`](#func-app-expectclosed), [`App.ExpectWindowCount`](#func-app-expectwindowcount) and [`App.ExpectNoWindow`](#func-app-expectnowindow). What the user does with the window manager: [`App.RequestClose`](#func-app-requestclose) (the close button), [`App.Minimize`](#func-app-minimize), [`App.Maximize`](#func-app-maximize), [`App.Unmaximize`](#func-app-unmaximize), [`App.SetFullscreen`](#func-app-setfullscreen), [`App.Restore`](#func-app-restore), [`App.MoveWindow`](#func-app-movewindow), [`App.Resize`](#func-app-resize) and [`App.BringToFront`](#func-app-bringtofront). A window blocked by a modal one drops input.

Custom title bars: [`App.HitRegions`](#func-app-hitregions) and [`App.HitAt`](#func-app-hitat) read the regions h.WindowDrag and h.WindowControl send to the OS, a click on the drag area ([`App.Click`](#func-app-click), [`App.ClickAt`](#func-app-clickat), [`App.DoubleClick`](#func-app-doubleclick)) is the OS's press ([`App.CaptionDrags`](#func-app-captiondrags), [`App.WindowMenus`](#func-app-windowmenus), a double click maximizes), and the controls are buttons that act on click. A [`TitleBarOverlay`](#func-titlebaroverlay) window keeps the OS's buttons over the content where the test says ([`TitleBarControls`](#func-titlebarcontrols), [`App.SetTitleBarControls`](#func-app-settitlebarcontrols), [`MacTitleBarControls`](#variables) under [`PlatformKeys`](#func-platformkeys) ("darwin")): [`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate).TitleBarControls reports them.

Transparent windows: a [`Transparent`](#func-transparent) window's screenshots and goldens keep the alpha of the frame (a PNG with transparent pixels where the app paints nothing), and pointer actions over its (nearly) transparent pixels go to what is below the window, as on the desktop: they reach nothing ([`App.TakesInput`](#func-app-takesinput)). [`NoCompositing`](#func-nocompositing) and [`App.SetCompositing`](#func-app-setcompositing) play a desktop that cannot show transparency (X11 without a compositing manager), where the window is opaque.

The app's menu bar (desktop.AppMenuBar): [`App.AppMenuBar`](#func-app-appmenubar), [`App.AppMenuItems`](#func-app-appmenuitems) and [`App.ChooseAppMenuItem`](#func-app-chooseappmenuitem). The headless desktop has the platform's app bar by default, as macOS; [`WithUnsupported`](#func-withunsupported) and [`App.Unsupported`](#func-app-unsupported) with [`AppMenu`](#type-desktopservice) play Windows (every framed window gets the bar) and, with [`NativeMenus`](#type-desktopservice) too, Linux. kit's menus stay drawn unless [`PreferNativeMenus`](#func-prefernativemenus).

Quitting: [`App.ExpectQuit`](#func-app-expectquit) waits for tela.Quit or a close request of the main window without an OnClose; the app is then over, as when tela.Main returns: every window unmounted, the cleanups of the effects run, and further use fails the test. [`App.HasQuit`](#func-app-hasquit) and [`App.ExpectRunning`](#func-app-expectrunning) check that it did or did not. [`App.RequestQuit`](#func-app-requestquit) plays the OS asking the app to quit (macOS's Cmd+Q: [`OnQuit`](#func-onquit)). The window options ([`Title`](#func-title), [`MinSize`](#func-minsize), [`MaxSize`](#func-maxsize), [`FixedSize`](#func-fixedsize), [`Frameless`](#func-frameless), [`TitleBarOverlay`](#func-titlebaroverlay), [`Transparent`](#func-transparent), [`AlwaysOnTop`](#func-alwaysontop), [`TitleBar`](#func-titlebar), [`Backdrop`](#func-backdrop), [`StartHidden`](#func-starthidden), [`Icon`](#func-icon), [`Placement`](#func-placement), [`OnClose`](#func-onclose), [`OnQuit`](#func-onquit), [`Screen`](#func-screen)) set the main window's fields for Mount.

### Drag and drop

The headless backend plays the operating system's part in HTML drag and drop. [`App.DragTo`](#func-app-dragto) drags an h.Draggable element to another element, [`App.DragToWindow`](#func-app-dragtowindow) to one in another window of the app, and [`App.DropOutside`](#func-app-dropoutside) ends a drag in another application; [`App.DropFiles`](#func-app-dropfiles) and [`App.DropData`](#func-app-dropdata) drop what another application drags (build it with [`DragFiles`](#func-dragfiles), [`DragText`](#func-dragtext), [`DragHTML`](#func-draghtml), [`DragPNG`](#func-dragpng), [`DragType`](#func-dragtype)). They return the effect the app accepted, tela.DropNone for a refusal. The steps they are made of can be used alone, to test drag-over styling or inspect the data: [`App.StartDrag`](#func-app-startdrag), [`App.HoverDrag`](#func-app-hoverdrag), [`App.LeaveDrag`](#func-app-leavedrag), [`App.CancelDrag`](#func-app-canceldrag), [`App.DropOn`](#func-app-dropon) and [`App.ActiveDrag`](#func-app-activedrag); the options [`Carrying`](#func-carrying), [`Allowed`](#func-allowed), [`Modifiers`](#func-modifiers) and [`Steps`](#func-steps) shape them.

```go
app.DropFiles(telatest.ByTestID("upload"), filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "photo.png"))
app.StartDrag(telatest.ByTestID("card-7"))
app.HoverDrag(telatest.ByTestID("column-done"))
app.ExpectText("Release to move here")
app.DropOn(telatest.ByTestID("column-done"))
```

### System settings

[`App.SetDarkMode`](#func-app-setdarkmode), [`App.SetReducedMotion`](#func-app-setreducedmotion), [`App.SetHighContrast`](#func-app-sethighcontrast), [`App.SetTextScale`](#func-app-settextscale), [`App.SetAccentColor`](#func-app-setaccentcolor) and [`App.ClearAccentColor`](#func-app-clearaccentcolor) change what the system says while the app is mounted, as the user does in the system's settings; the components that read the setting rebuild. The options [`Dark`](#func-dark), [`ReducedMotion`](#func-reducedmotion), [`HighContrast`](#func-highcontrast), [`TextScale`](#func-textscale) and [`AccentColor`](#func-accentcolor) set it at Mount.

[`PlatformKeys`](#func-platformkeys) gives the app another platform's key conventions (the text fields' bindings, the events' CmdOrCtrl, what "ControlOrMeta" presses), so a test of Command shortcuts runs on any OS.

### The clock

The window's clock is manual: it starts at zero and moves only when the app waits or the test advances it, so animations, scroll flings and timers are deterministic. Frames are paced like a 60 Hz display.

### Goldens and snapshots

[`App.Golden`](#func-app-golden) compares the window's pixels with testdata/\<name\>, bit by bit unless a [`Tolerance`](#func-tolerance) is given (Tela renders the same pixels on every platform, ADR-027); [`App.GoldenScales`](#func-app-goldenscales) makes one golden per display scale. TELA_UPDATE=1 go test regenerates goldens (ADR-022). [`App.AriaSnapshot`](#func-app-ariasnapshot) returns the YAML that `tela inspect` prints, and [`App.ExpectAria`](#func-app-expectaria) and [`App.AriaGolden`](#func-app-ariagolden) compare it.

### Debug overlays

[`Debug`](#func-debug) turns on the overlays of TELA_DEBUG (layout, paint-flash, layers, fps, semantics) in a mounted app or a headless render, so a golden shows them. The environment variable itself is ignored: a test only gets overlays it asks for. A paint flash fades over 300 ms of app time and the fps meter redraws on every frame; neither keeps actions waiting, so use [`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance) to look at them, and [`DebugClock`](#func-debugclock) to script the frame times the meter shows.

### Headless rendering without a test

[`Render`](#func-render), [`AriaSnapshot`](#func-ariasnapshot) and [`LayoutJSON`](#func-layoutjson) mount a tree, run frames until it is quiet and return the image, the aria snapshot or the layout JSON, for tools. `tela snapshot` and `tela inspect` are built on them.

## Constants

```go
const (
    // HitClient is ordinary content: what lies outside every region, and
    // what a hole in a drag region is.
    HitClient = platform.HitClient
    // HitCaption is a drag area (h.WindowDrag): the OS handles presses in
    // it (move, double click to maximize, window menu).
    HitCaption = platform.HitCaption
    // HitMinimize, HitMaximize and HitClose are the window-control buttons
    // (h.WindowControl): events over them reach the app as usual.
    HitMinimize = platform.HitMinimize
    HitMaximize = platform.HitMaximize
    HitClose    = platform.HitClose
    // HitResizeTop to HitResizeBottomRight are the resize handles of
    // h.WindowResize along a side or at a corner: a press there resizes
    // the window from that edge (see [App.ResizeStarts]).
    HitResizeTop         = platform.HitResizeTop
    HitResizeBottom      = platform.HitResizeBottom
    HitResizeLeft        = platform.HitResizeLeft
    HitResizeRight       = platform.HitResizeRight
    HitResizeTopLeft     = platform.HitResizeTopLeft
    HitResizeTopRight    = platform.HitResizeTopRight
    HitResizeBottomLeft  = platform.HitResizeBottomLeft
    HitResizeBottomRight = platform.HitResizeBottomRight
)
```

```go
const DefaultTimeout = 5 * time.Second
```

DefaultTimeout is how long actions and expectations wait for their condition when no [`Timeout`](#func-timeout) is given.

```go
const EnvCheckDamage = "TELA_CHECK_DAMAGE"
```

EnvCheckDamage is the environment variable that turns [`CheckDamage`](#func-checkdamage) on for every app ("1").

## Variables

```go
var MacTitleBarControls = tela.Rect{X: 9, Y: 13, Width: 60, Height: 14}
```

MacTitleBarControls is the rectangle of macOS's window buttons (the traffic lights) that [`TitleBarOverlay`](#func-titlebaroverlay) windows get under [`PlatformKeys`](#func-platformkeys)("darwin"): the place and size of the standard buttons centered in a 40 px title bar, in logical window coordinates, as macOS 26 places them on the macos-latest runner (AppKit's own place there is 9,9 60x14 in its 32 pt title bar).

## Functions

### func AriaSnapshot

```go
func AriaSnapshot(root tela.Component, opts ...Option) (yaml string, err error)
```

AriaSnapshot mounts root and returns its semantics tree as a Playwright aria snapshot, without a trailing newline: the YAML `tela inspect --aria` prints.

**Example**

```go
yaml, err := telatest.AriaSnapshot(tela.C(Counter))
if err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
fmt.Println(yaml)
// Output:
// - 'heading "Count: 0" [level=1]'
// - button "Increment"
```

### func LayoutJSON

```go
func LayoutJSON(root tela.Component, opts ...Option) (js []byte, err error)
```

LayoutJSON mounts root and returns its layout tree as indented JSON, one object per box with its border box, edges, text and computed style (paragraphs also with the fragments of their inline elements; atomic inlines with inlineBox), ending with a newline: the output of `tela inspect --layout`. rect is the box as layout placed it; a box that is painted elsewhere, because of a transform or scrolled content, also has bounds, the same shape: the bounding box of its transformed border box in window coordinates, as tela.ElementRef.Bounds returns it.

### func Render

```go
func Render(root tela.Component, opts ...Option) (img *image.RGBA, err error)
```

Render mounts root, lays it out and paints it at the configured size and scale (default 800x600 at scale 1) and returns the image, in physical pixels over the root's background (white by default). Effects run as in a window and then clean up; state passive effects set is rendered only when the tree needs further frames. root is a node or a component, as for [`Mount`](#func-mount); a Prop is an error.

**Example**

```go
img, err := telatest.Render(Div(Class("size-8 bg-black")),
    telatest.Size(16, 16), telatest.Scale(2))
if err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
fmt.Println(img.Bounds().Dx(), img.Bounds().Dy(), img.RGBAAt(2, 2))
// Output: 32 32 {0 0 0 255}
```

### func TempDesktopDirs

```go
func TempDesktopDirs(tb testing.TB) string
```

TempDesktopDirs points package desktop's folders (ConfigDir, the settings store, saved window placements...) at a new temporary directory for the rest of the test, through the desktop.DirEnv variable, and returns it. Call it before the app reads a setting. Like t.Setenv, it cannot be used in parallel tests.

## Types

### type App

```go
type App struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

App is a UI mounted in a headless window: Tela's real pipeline and event dispatch with a window that is a record in memory and a clock that only moves when the app waits or the test calls [`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance).

Actions and expectations settle the app first: they apply the pending state updates and run frames, advancing the clock to each frame, until nothing is dirty and no animation or scroll fling is running. A held pointer's long-press timer, and the fade of overlay scrollbars, fire only when the clock reaches them, with [`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance) or while an expectation waits.

An App must be used from the goroutine of its test; the state setters and tela.Post may be called from any goroutine.

#### func Mount

```go
func Mount(tb testing.TB, root tela.Component, opts ...Option) *App
```

Mount shows root in a headless window and returns the running app. The window starts focused, so key events reach the focused element; it is unmounted when the test ends, running the cleanups of its effects. root is a node or a component: a struct component value, or a function component through its public wrapper, a function that returns its tela.C or tela.CP node (or use [`MountFunc`](#func-mountfunc)). A [`tela.Preview`](API-Reference-tela#type-preview)'s Theme and ColorScheme apply after the options, as in `tela snapshot`.

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, Counter(), telatest.Size(400, 300))
app := telatest.Mount(t, Card{Title: "Inbox"})
```

Mount makes the app receive the functions given to tela.Post, which are delivered to one tree per process: do not mount apps that use Post from parallel tests.

The windows a tela.Window opens are opened in the headless backend too, by a fake window manager. The returned App is scoped to the main window; [`App.Windows`](#func-app-windows), [`App.Window`](#func-app-window) and [`App.WaitForWindow`](#func-app-waitforwindow) give an App scoped to each of the others, with the same queries, actions, snapshots and goldens (see "Windows" in the package documentation).

**Example**

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(Counter), telatest.Size(400, 300))

app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment"))
app.ExpectText("Count: 1")

fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - 'heading "Count: 1" [level=1]'
// - button "Increment"
```

#### func MountApp

```go
func MountApp(tb testing.TB, app tela.App, opts ...Option) *App
```

MountApp shows app.Root in a headless window configured like the app, the way [`tela.Main`](API-Reference-tela#func-main) shows it in a real one, and returns the running app. The size, root class, color scheme, theme, class aliases, scrollbar and scroll settings and Dev of the app apply (see [`FromApp`](#func-fromapp)), and so do the fields of the OS window: Title, AppID, the size limits, FixedSize, Frameless, AlwaysOnTop, Hidden, Icon, Placement and OnClose (see [`Title`](#func-title), [`MinSize`](#func-minsize), [`Frameless`](#func-frameless), [`StartHidden`](#func-starthidden), [`Placement`](#func-placement) and [`OnClose`](#func-onclose), the options that set them by hand). A Hidden app starts with its window hidden, and without an OnClose the app quits when its main window is asked to close ([`App.RequestClose`](#func-app-requestclose), [`App.ExpectQuit`](#func-app-expectquit)). The options override all of them. It fails the test when app.Root is nil.

```go
var App = tela.App{Title: "Notes", Width: 900, Height: 600, Root: Notes()}

func main() { tela.Main(App) }

func TestNotes(t *testing.T) {
    app := telatest.MountApp(t, App) // the same window as main's
    app.ExpectText("Notes")
}
```

`tela snapshot` and `tela inspect` read the same package-level `var App`. See [`Mount`](#func-mount) for what the app does and when it ends.

**Example**

```go
// The App that main passes to tela.Main, and that `tela snapshot` reads
// from the package.
app := telatest.MountApp(t, tela.App{
    Title:     "Counter",
    Width:     480,
    Height:    320,
    RootClass: "bg-slate-100",
    Root:      tela.C(Counter),
})

app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment"))
app.ExpectText("Count: 1")
fmt.Println(app.Screenshot().Bounds().Size()) // the App's window
// Output: (480,320)
```

#### func MountFunc

```go
func MountFunc(tb testing.TB, fn func() tela.Node, opts ...Option) *App
```

MountFunc shows the component fn in a headless window and returns the running app: it is Mount(tb, tela.C(fn), opts...), for the common case of a test that mounts one component.

```go
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, Counter, telatest.Size(400, 300))
```

See [`Mount`](#func-mount) for what the app does and when it ends.

**Example**

```go
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, Counter, telatest.Size(400, 300))

app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment"))
app.ExpectText("Count: 1")
fmt.Println(app.Count(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment")))
// Output: 1
```

#### func (*App) ActiveDrag

```go
func (a *App) ActiveDrag() (DragInfo, bool)
```

ActiveDrag returns the drag in progress: the one [`App.StartDrag`](#func-app-startdrag) began from an h.Draggable element, or another application's ([`Carrying`](#func-carrying)), until a drop, a cancel or [`App.DropOutside`](#func-app-dropoutside).

```go
app.StartDrag(telatest.ByTestID("card-7"))
info, _ := app.ActiveDrag()
if got := info.Data.GetData("application/x-card"); got != "7" { ... }
```

#### func (*App) Advance

```go
func (a *App) Advance(d time.Duration)
```

Advance runs the app's clock forward by d: the frames, animations, scroll animations and flings, long-press timers and other deadlines that fall within d happen in order, each frame at its own time. It does not settle the app afterwards: work requested at the very end is handled by the next action, expectation or Advance.

**Example**

```go
// The clock is manual: a long press fires when the app's time gets
// to 500 ms, whatever the machine's speed.
pressed := func() tela.Node {
    long, setLong := tela.UseState(false)
    return Button(OnLongPress(func(tela.PointerEvent) { setLong.Set(true) }),
        IfElse(long, Text("Held"), Text("Press and hold")))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(pressed))

app.Hover(telatest.ByRole("button", ""))
app.MouseDown()
app.Advance(600 * time.Millisecond)
app.MouseUp()
app.ExpectText("Held")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output: - button "Held"
```

#### func (*App) AnswerFileDialog

```go
func (a *App) AnswerFileDialog(paths ...string)
```

AnswerFileDialog answers the oldest open file dialog as the user would: with the given paths, or, without paths, by canceling it. The app's callback runs and the app settles. It fails the test when no file dialog is open, or when a dialog that takes one path gets several.

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open…"))
app.AnswerFileDialog("/home/ana/notes/groceries.md")
app.ExpectText("groceries.md")
```

#### func (*App) AnswerMessage

```go
func (a *App) AnswerMessage(answer desktop.Answer)
```

AnswerMessage answers the oldest open message box with the button answer, as the user would (a drawn box gets a real click on its button); the app's callback runs and the app settles. It fails the test when no box is open or the box has no such button.

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Close"))
app.AnswerMessage(desktop.AnswerNo) // "Save the changes?" — No
```

#### func (*App) AppMenuBar

```go
func (a *App) AppMenuBar() []MenuItem
```

AppMenuBar returns the app's menu bar (a mounted desktop.AppMenuBar) as the platform has it, nil without one, after settling the app. Where the platform has no app bar but windows have menu bars (Windows; [`WithUnsupported`](#func-withunsupported)(AppMenu)), it is the bar of this App's window, which App.MenuBar returns too. The app items are [`App.AppMenuItems`](#func-app-appmenuitems).

#### func (*App) AppMenuItems

```go
func (a *App) AppMenuItems() []MenuItem
```

AppMenuItems returns the items the app gave macOS's app menu (desktop.AppMenuBar.AppItems), after settling the app. They are empty where the platform ignores them.

#### func (*App) AriaGolden

```go
func (a *App) AriaGolden(name string)
```

AriaGolden compares the app's aria snapshot, with a final newline (what `tela inspect` prints), with the text file testdata/\<name\> (TELA_UPDATE=1 writes it). Use it for snapshots too long to write in the test; [`App.ExpectAria`](#func-app-expectaria) is better for short ones.

#### func (*App) AriaSnapshot

```go
func (a *App) AriaSnapshot() string
```

AriaSnapshot returns the app's semantics tree as a Playwright aria snapshot, the YAML that `tela inspect` prints, without a trailing newline, after settling the app (under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), handling only the work due: running animations stay where they are). For a counter:

```go
snap := app.AriaSnapshot()
// - heading "Count: 1" [level=1]
// - button "Increment"
```

#### func (*App) Backdrop

```go
func (a *App) Backdrop() tela.Backdrop
```

Backdrop returns the system backdrop the window has asked the OS for (tela.App.Backdrop, tela.Window.Backdrop).

#### func (*App) BackendStrings

```go
func (a *App) BackendStrings() map[string]string
```

BackendStrings returns the texts the app gave the platform to show itself in its language (the labels of native message boxes, of the macOS menus and of the save panel; ADR-251), after settling the app: only the IDs the app translated (see [`tela.Labels`](API-Reference-tela#func-labels)), nil with none.

#### func (*App) Blocked

```go
func (a *App) Blocked() bool
```

Blocked reports whether a visible modal window blocks this one; see [`App.BlockedBy`](#func-app-blockedby).

#### func (*App) BlockedBy

```go
func (a *App) BlockedBy() *App
```

BlockedBy returns the visible modal window that blocks this one, or nil. A blocked window takes no input: core drops it (after cancelling the pointers) and a press in it activates the modal window, and a request to close it is refused.

#### func (*App) Blocks

```go
func (a *App) Blocks() *App
```

Blocks returns the window a modal window blocks while it is visible: its parent. It is nil for a window that is not modal, or hidden.

#### func (*App) Bounds

```go
func (a *App) Bounds(l Locator) tela.Rect
```

Bounds returns the border box of the element l locates, in logical pixels from the window's top-left corner, after transforms and scroll offsets: the same rectangle as tela.ElementRef.Bounds. For an inline element it bounds its text.

```go
r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByRole("button", "Save"))
if r.Width < 80 { t.Errorf("the button is %gpx wide", r.Width) }
```

#### func (*App) BringToFront

```go
func (a *App) BringToFront()
```

BringToFront activates the window as the user does by clicking its task bar entry: it comes back from minimized and, when it is visible, takes the keyboard focus from the other windows. The pointer and key actions do it by themselves, as clicking or typing in a window does. Playwright's page.bringToFront().

#### func (*App) CancelDrag

```go
func (a *App) CancelDrag()
```

CancelDrag cancels the drag in progress, as the user pressing Escape does: OnDragLeave runs on the window it is over, and the source's OnDragEnd runs with DropNone.

#### func (*App) CaptionDrags

```go
func (a *App) CaptionDrags() int
```

CaptionDrags returns how many presses in a caption region started a move of the window by the fake window manager: a primary press that is not the second of a double click. A press in a caption region is the OS's: the app does not see it or the rest of its pointer sequence. Drive one with [`App.Click`](#func-app-click) on an element inside an h.WindowDrag region, or [`App.ClickAt`](#func-app-clickat).

#### func (*App) ChooseAppMenuItem

```go
func (a *App) ChooseAppMenuItem(path ...string)
```

ChooseAppMenuItem chooses an item of the app's menu bar, named by the labels from the top-level entry down, as the user does with the mouse: its OnSelect runs and the app settles. An item of macOS's app menu is named by its label alone ([`App.AppMenuItems`](#func-app-appmenuitems)). Role items are reported like any item, as on a platform without the role's native action, so the app carries them out (Copy acts on the focused field). Where the platform has no app bar but windows have menu bars (Windows; [`WithUnsupported`](#func-withunsupported)(AppMenu)), it chooses from this App's window's bar. It fails the test when the app has no menu bar, or the item is missing, disabled or opens a submenu.

```go
app.ChooseAppMenuItem("File", "New Note")
app.ChooseAppMenuItem("Settings…")
```

#### func (*App) ChooseMenuItem

```go
func (a *App) ChooseMenuItem(path ...string)
```

ChooseMenuItem chooses an item of the window's native menu bar, named by the labels from the top-level entry down, as the user does with the mouse or Alt: its OnSelect runs and the app settles. It fails the test when the window has no menu bar, or the item is missing, disabled or opens a submenu.

```go
app.ChooseMenuItem("File", "New")
```

#### func (*App) ChoosePopupItem

```go
func (a *App) ChoosePopupItem(path ...string)
```

ChoosePopupItem chooses an item of the open native context menu (the oldest, if several), named by its label, and for an item in a submenu by the labels of the submenus first, as ClickTrayItem does: its OnSelect runs, then the menu's done, and the app settles. It fails the test when no menu is open, or the item is missing, disabled, or opens a submenu.

```go
app.RightClick(telatest.ByText("groceries.md"))
app.ChoosePopupItem("Rename…")
```

#### func (*App) ClearAccentColor

```go
func (a *App) ClearAccentColor()
```

ClearAccentColor makes the system report no accent color, as a desktop without one does.

#### func (*App) Click

```go
func (a *App) Click(l Locator, opts ...ClickOption)
```

Click moves the pointer to the center of the element l locates, presses the primary button and releases it: real pointer events (hover, :active, focus on press, the gesture arena and the click), not a call to the handler. Each Click is a first click (ClickCount 1) even right after another, as in Playwright; use [`App.DoubleClick`](#func-app-doubleclick) for two. It waits for the element to be visible, enabled, in view and not covered by another element, and fails the test when l matches none or several. With [`Right`](#func-right) it presses the secondary button instead (the element's OnContextMenu runs, not its OnClick); [`App.Tap`](#func-app-tap) and [`App.LongPress`](#func-app-longpress) are the touch counterparts.

#### func (*App) ClickAt

```go
func (a *App) ClickAt(x, y float32, opts ...ClickOption)
```

ClickAt clicks at the point (x, y) of the window, in logical pixels from its top-left corner, with the same real pointer events as [`App.Click`](#func-app-click) (hover, :active, focus on press, the gesture arena and the click) but without looking for an element: whatever is under the point receives them, like a user clicking there. It is for what a locator cannot name (a canvas, a chart, a drop zone found with [`App.Bounds`](#func-app-bounds)) and fails the test when the point is outside the window. [`Right`](#func-right) clicks with the secondary button, to open a context menu at a point.

```go
r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("chart"))
app.ClickAt(r.X+r.Width/2, r.Y+10)
app.ClickAt(r.X+20, r.Y+20, telatest.Right())
```

**Example**

```go
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, Counter, telatest.Size(400, 300))

r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment"))
app.ClickAt(r.X+r.Width/2, r.Y+r.Height/2)
app.ExpectText("Count: 1")
fmt.Println("clicked")
// Output: clicked
```

#### func (*App) ClickNotification

```go
func (a *App) ClickNotification(title string)
```

ClickNotification clicks the open notification with the given title (the newest, if several): its OnClick runs and it closes.

#### func (*App) ClickNotificationAction

```go
func (a *App) ClickNotificationAction(title, action string)
```

ClickNotificationAction clicks the button labeled action of the open notification with the given title: the action's OnClick runs and the notification closes.

#### func (*App) ClickTray

```go
func (a *App) ClickTray()
```

ClickTray clicks the app's tray icon (its OnClick runs). It fails the test unless the app shows exactly one.

#### func (*App) ClickTrayItem

```go
func (a *App) ClickTrayItem(path ...string)
```

ClickTrayItem chooses an item of the tray icon's menu (its OnSelect runs), named by its label, and for an item in a submenu by the labels of the submenus first:

```go
app.ClickTrayItem("Quit")
app.ClickTrayItem("Theme", "Dark")
```

It fails the test when the app does not show exactly one tray icon, or the item is missing, disabled, or opens a submenu.

#### func (*App) Clipboard

```go
func (a *App) Clipboard() *tela.DataTransfer
```

Clipboard returns a copy of the clipboard's content, after settling the app: what the app wrote (desktop.WriteClipboard, a text field's copy), or what SetClipboard put there.

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Copy link"))
if got := app.Clipboard().Text(); got != "notes:open?id=3" {
    t.Errorf("clipboard = %q", got)
}
```

#### func (*App) Close

```go
func (a *App) Close()
```

Close unmounts the whole app now (every window, not only the one this App is scoped to), running the cleanups of its effects. The test does it when it ends; call it to test unmounting. Using the app afterwards fails the test. To test what the user closing a window does, use [`App.RequestClose`](#func-app-requestclose).

#### func (*App) Closed

```go
func (a *App) Closed() bool
```

Closed reports whether the window is closed: it unmounted (its tela.Window left the tree, or the user's close request was granted) or the app ended.

#### func (*App) Count

```go
func (a *App) Count(l Locator) int
```

Count returns how many elements l matches now, after settling the app (under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), handling only the work due: running animations stay where they are). It does not wait.

#### func (*App) Cursor

```go
func (a *App) Cursor() string
```

Cursor returns the CSS name of the mouse cursor the window shows ("default", "pointer", "not-allowed"...), after settling the app (under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), handling only the work due).

#### func (*App) DismissNotification

```go
func (a *App) DismissNotification(title string)
```

DismissNotification closes the open notification with the given title as the user does with its close button (or as it expires): its OnClose runs.

#### func (*App) DismissPopupMenu

```go
func (a *App) DismissPopupMenu()
```

DismissPopupMenu closes the open native context menu without choosing (Escape, a click elsewhere): the menu's done runs with chosen false.

#### func (*App) DoubleClick

```go
func (a *App) DoubleClick(l Locator)
```

DoubleClick clicks the element twice in a row, so the second click has a click count of 2 and OnDoubleClick runs. See [`App.Click`](#func-app-click).

#### func (*App) Drag

```go
func (a *App) Drag(from, to Locator, opts ...DragOption)
```

Drag presses the primary button at the center of from, moves the pointer in steps to the center of to, and releases it there: a real drag through the gesture arena (OnDragStart, OnDrag, OnDragEnd), the pointer capture and the hover states of the elements on the way. The center of to is read once the drag has started.

#### func (*App) DragBy

```go
func (a *App) DragBy(l Locator, dx, dy float32, opts ...DragOption)
```

DragBy drags the element l locates by (dx, dy) logical pixels from its center. See [`App.Drag`](#func-app-drag).

#### func (*App) DragFromTo

```go
func (a *App) DragFromTo(from, to tela.Point, opts ...DragOption)
```

DragFromTo presses the primary button at the point from, moves the pointer in steps to the point to and releases it there, in logical pixels from the window's top-left corner: the drag of [`App.Drag`](#func-app-drag) without locators, for sources and targets a locator cannot name (a canvas, a slider track at a given value). It fails the test when a point is outside the window.

```go
r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("track"))
app.DragFromTo(tela.Point{X: r.X + 4, Y: r.Y + 8}, tela.Point{X: r.X + r.Width/2, Y: r.Y + 8})
```

**Example**

```go
moved := 0
area := func() tela.Node {
    return Div(Class("size-32 bg-slate-200"),
        OnDrag(func(e tela.DragEvent) { moved = int(e.OffsetX) }))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, area, telatest.Size(200, 200))

app.DragFromTo(tela.Point{X: 10, Y: 10}, tela.Point{X: 90, Y: 10})
fmt.Println(moved)
// Output: 80
```

#### func (*App) DragTo

```go
func (a *App) DragTo(from, to Locator, opts ...DragOption) tela.DropEffect
```

DragTo drags the element from locates, which must be h.Draggable(true), to the element to locates in the same window and drops it there, like Playwright's locator.dragTo, through the app's drag and drop handlers ([`App.StartDrag`](#func-app-startdrag), [`App.HoverDrag`](#func-app-hoverdrag), [`App.DropOn`](#func-app-dropon)). It returns the effect the target accepted, tela.DropNone when it refused; the source's OnDragEnd got the same one.

```go
app.DragTo(telatest.ByTestID("card-7"), telatest.ByTestID("column-done"))
app.ExpectText("Card 7")
```

For the gesture drag of OnDrag (sliders, movable panels) use [`App.Drag`](#func-app-drag).

#### func (*App) DragToWindow

```go
func (a *App) DragToWindow(from Locator, window *App, to Locator, opts ...DragOption) tela.DropEffect
```

DragToWindow drags the element from locates to the element to locates in another window of the app, window (an App from [`App.Windows`](#func-app-windows), [`App.Window`](#func-app-window) or [`App.WaitForWindow`](#func-app-waitforwindow)), and drops it there ([`App.DragTo`](#func-app-dragto)).

```go
app.DragToWindow(telatest.ByTestID("tab-1"), app.Window("Detached"), telatest.ByTestID("tabs"))
```

#### func (*App) DropData

```go
func (a *App) DropData(l Locator, payload DragPayload, opts ...DragOption) tela.DropEffect
```

DropData drops payload from another application on the element l locates, and returns the effect the app accepted ([`App.DropOn`](#func-app-dropon)).

```go
app.DropData(telatest.ByTestID("editor"), telatest.DragHTML("<b>Hi</b>").And(telatest.DragText("Hi")))
```

#### func (*App) DropFiles

```go
func (a *App) DropFiles(l Locator, paths ...string) tela.DropEffect
```

DropFiles drops files from a file manager on the element l locates, and returns the effect the app accepted ([`App.DropOn`](#func-app-dropon)). The paths must be absolute.

```go
path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "photo.png")
if app.DropFiles(telatest.ByTestID("upload"), path) == tela.DropNone { t.Fatal("refused") }
app.ExpectText("photo.png")
```

#### func (*App) DropOn

```go
func (a *App) DropOn(l Locator, opts ...DragOption) tela.DropEffect
```

DropOn releases the drag in progress over the center of the element l locates, after moving it there as [`App.HoverDrag`](#func-app-hoverdrag) does, and returns the effect the app accepted: tela.DropNone when it did not take the drop, tela.DropCopy, DropMove or DropLink when it did. An app takes a drop when its latest OnDragOver on the way called PreventDefault with an effect the source allows (a drag with [`Carrying`](#func-carrying) allows copy, move and link unless [`Allowed`](#func-allowed) says otherwise), and OnDrop did not set DropNone. A refused drop runs OnDragLeave instead of OnDrop. The source's OnDragEnd runs with the same effect.

```go
effect := app.DropOn(telatest.ByRole("region", "Inbox"), telatest.Carrying(telatest.DragText("hello")))
if effect != tela.DropCopy { t.Fatalf("the inbox did not copy the text: %v", effect) }
```

#### func (*App) DropOutside

```go
func (a *App) DropOutside(effect tela.DropEffect)
```

DropOutside ends the drag the app started over another application, which performs effect: the source's OnDragEnd runs with it. Pass tela.DropNone for an application that refuses it. effect must be one the drag allows (its DataTransfer.EffectAllowed).

```go
app.StartDrag(telatest.ByTestID("card-7"))
app.DropOutside(tela.DropMove)
app.ExpectNoText("Card 7") // OnDragEnd removed the moved card
```

#### func (*App) Expect

```go
func (a *App) Expect(l Locator, states ...State)
```

Expect waits until the element l locates satisfies every state, like Playwright's toBeChecked, toBeDisabled and toBeExpanded: it settles the app and checks, and while a state does not hold lets a frame of app time pass and checks again, until it holds or the [`Timeout`](#func-timeout) expires. The locator must match exactly one element (strictness). The failure message says which states differ, shows the element's actual states and its line of the aria snapshot.

```go
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("switch", "Wi-Fi"), telatest.Checked(true), telatest.Disabled(false))
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("button", "Menu"), telatest.Expanded(true))
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Email"), telatest.HasValue("ada@example.com"))
```

**Example**

```go
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, Settings, telatest.Size(400, 400))

wifi := telatest.ByRole("switch", "Wi-Fi")
app.Expect(wifi, telatest.Checked(false))
app.Click(wifi)
app.Expect(wifi, telatest.Checked(true), telatest.Disabled(false))
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("button", "Save"), telatest.Disabled(true))
fmt.Println("ok")
// Output: ok
```

#### func (*App) ExpectAria

```go
func (a *App) ExpectAria(yaml string)
```

ExpectAria waits until the window's aria snapshot equals yaml (see [`App.AriaSnapshot`](#func-app-ariasnapshot)), like Playwright's toMatchAriaSnapshot in exact mode: after trimming the surrounding blank lines and removing the indentation common to all lines, so a raw string can be indented like the code around it.

```go
app.ExpectAria(`
    - heading "Count: 1" [level=1]
    - button "Increment"
`)
```

**Example**

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(Counter))
app.Click(telatest.ByText("Increment"))

// The expected snapshot may be indented like the code around it.
app.ExpectAria(`
    - 'heading "Count: 1" [level=1]'
    - button "Increment"
`)
fmt.Println("matches")
// Output: matches
```

#### func (*App) ExpectClosed

```go
func (a *App) ExpectClosed()
```

ExpectClosed waits until the window is closed (see [`App.Closed`](#func-app-closed)) and fails the test at the timeout. A close request the app refuses (a tela.Window whose OnClose does not update the state that renders it) leaves the window open.

#### func (*App) ExpectCount

```go
func (a *App) ExpectCount(l Locator, n int)
```

ExpectCount waits until l matches exactly n elements.

#### func (*App) ExpectFocused

```go
func (a *App) ExpectFocused(l Locator)
```

ExpectFocused waits until the element l locates has the keyboard focus.

#### func (*App) ExpectNoText

```go
func (a *App) ExpectNoText(text string)
```

ExpectNoText waits until the window does not show text (see [`App.ExpectText`](#func-app-expecttext)).

#### func (*App) ExpectNoWindow

```go
func (a *App) ExpectNoWindow(title string)
```

ExpectNoWindow waits until no open window has the title, and fails the test at the timeout.

#### func (*App) ExpectQuit

```go
func (a *App) ExpectQuit()
```

ExpectQuit waits until the app quits (see [`App.HasQuit`](#func-app-hasquit)) and fails the test at the timeout. Once the app quit, its windows are unmounted and the cleanups of their effects have run, so the test can assert them.

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Quit"))   // OnClick(tela.Quit)
app.ExpectQuit()
if !cleaned { t.Error("the effect did not clean up") }
```

#### func (*App) ExpectRole

```go
func (a *App) ExpectRole(role, name string)
```

ExpectRole waits until an element with the role and accessible name is visible (see [`ByRole`](#func-byrole); an empty name accepts any). It passes when one or more elements match: use [`App.ExpectCount`](#func-app-expectcount) to assert there is exactly one.

```go
app.ExpectRole("heading", "Settings")
```

#### func (*App) ExpectRunning

```go
func (a *App) ExpectRunning()
```

ExpectRunning fails the test when the app quit (see [`App.HasQuit`](#func-app-hasquit)): the check of an OnClose that hides the window to keep the app in the tray.

#### func (*App) ExpectText

```go
func (a *App) ExpectText(text string)
```

ExpectText waits until the window shows text: it is contained in the window's text content (whitespace normalized, hidden elements left out, block boundaries counting as spaces; case sensitive).

```go
app.ExpectText("Count: 1")
```

#### func (*App) ExpectTitle

```go
func (a *App) ExpectTitle(title string)
```

ExpectTitle waits until the window's title is title.

#### func (*App) ExpectValue

```go
func (a *App) ExpectValue(l Locator, value string)
```

ExpectValue waits until the text field l locates holds value (Playwright's toHaveValue).

```go
app.Type("hello")
app.ExpectValue(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Message"), "hello")
```

#### func (*App) ExpectWindowCount

```go
func (a *App) ExpectWindowCount(n int)
```

ExpectWindowCount waits until the app has n open windows (the main window counts), and fails the test at the timeout.

#### func (*App) ExpectWindowState

```go
func (a *App) ExpectWindowState(conds ...WindowCond)
```

ExpectWindowState waits until the window's state meets every condition, and fails the test at the timeout, showing the unmet conditions and the state it has.

```go
win.Maximize()
win.ExpectWindowState(telatest.Maximized(true), telatest.Minimized(false))
```

#### func (*App) FailSecrets

```go
func (a *App) FailSecrets(err error)
```

FailSecrets makes every secret call of the app fail with err from now on, until FailSecrets(nil): desktop.ErrSecretCanceled plays the user dismissing the keyring's unlock prompt. (A desktop without secure storage is App.Unsupported(telatest.Secrets).)

```go
app.FailSecrets(desktop.ErrSecretCanceled)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Unlock"))
app.ExpectText("The keyring stayed locked")
```

#### func (*App) FailShortcuts

```go
func (a *App) FailShortcuts(err error)
```

FailShortcuts makes every global shortcut the app registers from now on fail with err, until FailShortcuts(nil); shortcuts registered already keep their state. An error wrapping desktop.ErrAppNotRegistered plays a Linux desktop without the app's entry (desktop.RegisterApp). OnStatus gets ShortcutFailed with an error wrapping err.

```go
app.FailShortcuts(desktop.ErrAppNotRegistered)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("switch", "Quick note")) // registers again
```

#### func (*App) FailTrash

```go
func (a *App) FailTrash(err error)
```

FailTrash makes every desktop.MoveToTrash of the app fail with err from now on, until FailTrash(nil); the file stays in place: a file in use, a folder the user may not change. (A desktop without a trash, or a file it cannot take, is App.Unsupported(telatest.Trash).)

```go
app.FailTrash(errors.New("the file is in use"))
```

#### func (*App) FileDialogs

```go
func (a *App) FileDialogs() []FileDialog
```

FileDialogs returns the file dialogs open now, oldest first, after settling the app.

#### func (*App) Fill

```go
func (a *App) Fill(l Locator, text string)
```

Fill fills the text field l locates (an h.Input or h.Textarea) with text, like Playwright's fill: after the actionability checks of the pointer actions, it focuses the field, selects its value and replaces it with text as a single insertText edit (an empty text deletes the value), firing OnBeforeInput and OnChange once. MaxLength applies. It fails the test when the element is not an editable text field.

```go
app.Fill(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Email"), "ana@example.com")
```

Use [`App.Type`](#func-app-type) to send the characters one key at a time instead.

**Example**

```go
form := func() tela.Node {
    name, setName := tela.UseState("")
    return Div(
        Label(For("name"), Text("Name")),
        Input(ID("name"), Bind(name, setName)),
        P(Textf("Hello, %s!", name)),
    )
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(form))

app.Fill(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Name"), "Ada")
app.ExpectValue(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Name"), "Ada")
app.ExpectText("Hello, Ada!")
fmt.Println(app.Count(telatest.ByText("Hello, Ada!")))
// Output: 1
```

#### func (*App) Focus

```go
func (a *App) Focus(l Locator)
```

Focus gives the keyboard focus to the element l locates, like calling focus() on it: OnBlur and OnFocus run. It fails the test when the element cannot take the focus (give it a Button, TabIndex or an interactive role element).

#### func (*App) GlobalShortcuts

```go
func (a *App) GlobalShortcuts() []GlobalShortcut
```

GlobalShortcuts returns the global shortcuts the app has registered, in registration order, after settling the app.

#### func (*App) Golden

```go
func (a *App) Golden(name string, opts ...GoldenOption)
```

Golden compares the window's content, after settling the app (with [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), at the current time: see [`App.Screenshot`](#func-app-screenshot)), with the PNG testdata/\<name\> next to the test (a name without the ".png" extension gets it), bit by bit unless a [`Tolerance`](#func-tolerance) is given. TELA_UPDATE=1 writes the golden instead of comparing (ADR-022); review the PNG before committing it. On a mismatch, \<name\>\_actual.png and \<name\>\_diff.png are written next to the golden.

The picture is physical pixels, so a golden depends on [`Size`](#func-size) and [`Scale`](#func-scale); it also shows the overlay scrollbars while they are visible: advance the clock to hide them first when that matters.

#### func (*App) GoldenScales

```go
func (a *App) GoldenScales(name string, scales ...float64)
```

GoldenScales compares the window with one golden per display scale: testdata/\<name\>\_x\<scale\>.png, with the scale written like %g (name_x1.png, name_x2.png, name_x1.5.png), the naming of the examples' goldens. A name with the ".png" extension has it removed first. For each scale the window is moved to a display with that scale, as when a user drags it between monitors (the logical size is kept, the picture is size\*scale pixels), settled like [`App.Golden`](#func-app-golden) does, and compared; the app keeps its state and its original scale at the end. The comparison is bit by bit and TELA_UPDATE=1 writes the goldens, as with [`App.Golden`](#func-app-golden).

```go
app.GoldenScales("settings", 1, 2) // testdata/settings_x1.png, settings_x2.png
```

**Example**

GoldenScales has no output to check: it compares files in testdata.

```go
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, Counter, telatest.Size(400, 300))

// testdata/counter_x1.png and testdata/counter_x2.png; TELA_UPDATE=1
// writes them.
app.GoldenScales("counter", 1, 2)
```

#### func (*App) HasQuit

```go
func (a *App) HasQuit() bool
```

HasQuit reports whether the app quit: tela.Quit ran, or the main window was asked to close without a tela.App.OnClose. A quit app is over, as when tela.Main returns: every window was unmounted, so the cleanups of the effects ran, and using the app fails the test. The app is settled first.

#### func (*App) HitAt

```go
func (a *App) HitAt(x, y float32) HitKind
```

HitAt returns what the OS would find at the point (x, y), in logical pixels from the window's top-left corner: the kind of the last hit region that contains it, or [`HitClient`](#constants).

#### func (*App) HitRegions

```go
func (a *App) HitRegions() []HitRegion
```

HitRegions returns the hit regions the window sent to the OS, in order (later regions are on top): the drag areas, the holes in them, the window-control buttons and the resize handles that h.WindowDrag, h.WindowNoDrag, h.WindowControl and h.WindowResize mark. It is nil for a window without them.

#### func (*App) HoldAppEntry

```go
func (a *App) HoldAppEntry(id, path string)
```

HoldAppEntry plays another program's desktop entry of the app ID id (a package's), at path: desktop.RegisterApp then writes nothing unless it passes desktop.Replace, and desktop.AppStatus reports it. "" removes it.

#### func (*App) HoldAssociation

```go
func (a *App) HoldAssociation(as desktop.Association, other string)
```

HoldAssociation plays another application, named other, holding a: the app's desktop.Register of it fails with desktop.ErrAssociationTaken unless it passes desktop.Replace. "" releases it.

#### func (*App) Hover

```go
func (a *App) Hover(l Locator)
```

Hover moves the pointer to the center of the element l locates, so its hover: and group-hover: states apply. It waits for the element to be visible, in view and not covered.

#### func (*App) HoverDrag

```go
func (a *App) HoverDrag(l Locator, opts ...DragOption)
```

HoverDrag moves the drag in progress over the center of the element l locates and leaves it there, so the app can show its drag-over state: OnDragEnter on the element, OnDragLeave on the one it left, OnDragOver. The pointer moves in steps (default 12; [`Steps`](#func-steps)) when the drag is already over this window, and enters it directly otherwise.

With [`Carrying`](#func-carrying) it starts another application's drag first, over no window. The window need not be the drag's source: calling HoverDrag on the [`App`](#type-app) of another window of the app moves a drag between windows.

```go
app.HoverDrag(telatest.ByTestID("dropzone"), telatest.Carrying(telatest.DragFiles(path)))
app.ExpectText("Drop to upload")
app.LeaveDrag()
app.ExpectNoText("Drop to upload")
```

#### func (*App) InjectLaunch

```go
func (a *App) InjectLaunch(l desktop.Launch)
```

InjectLaunch plays the user starting the app again while it runs, as a single-instance app sees it (desktop.SingleInstance): the new process forwards l (its Args and Dir) and exits, the main window comes to the front (shown if hidden), and every desktop.UseLaunch handler gets the launch, with Source LaunchForwarded. With l.Source LaunchOpened it plays the OS opening links or files with the running app instead (macOS Launch Services: a link clicked, a file opened from the Finder), which needs no SingleInstance; with l.AtStart too, the file that started the app, as macOS hands it just after the start. The app settles.

```go
app := telatest.MountApp(t, desktop.SingleInstance(App))
app.InjectLaunch(desktop.Launch{Args: []string{"notes:open?id=3"}})
app.ExpectText("Groceries")
```

#### func (*App) LastWindow

```go
func (a *App) LastWindow() *App
```

LastWindow returns the newest open window: the one opened last, or the main window when it is the only one.

#### func (*App) LayoutJSON

```go
func (a *App) LayoutJSON() []byte
```

LayoutJSON returns the layout tree of the running app as indented JSON, ending with a newline, after settling it (under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), handling only the work due): the output of `tela inspect --layout` and of the function [`LayoutJSON`](#func-layoutjson), for the app as it is now, with the state its actions built up.

#### func (*App) LayoutJSONOf

```go
func (a *App) LayoutJSONOf(l Locator) []byte
```

LayoutJSONOf returns the layout subtree of the element l locates, in the same JSON as [`App.LayoutJSON`](#func-app-layoutjson) (indented, ending with a newline, rects in window coordinates before scroll offsets and transforms, with the painted "bounds" where they differ): the box of the element with everything inside it, as `tela inspect --layout` shows it at that place. An inline element, a text or a display: contents element gives the box of its nearest ancestor that has one. Like the other locator queries it settles the app first (under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), handling only the work due), and fails the test when l matches no element or several. tela mcp's inspect tool is built on it (ADR-194).

```go
js := app.LayoutJSONOf(telatest.ByRole("button", "Save"))
```

#### func (*App) LeaveDrag

```go
func (a *App) LeaveDrag()
```

LeaveDrag moves the drag in progress out of this window, as the pointer leaving it does: OnDragLeave runs. The drag goes on.

#### func (*App) LongPress

```go
func (a *App) LongPress(l Locator)
```

LongPress presses the element l locates with a finger at its center, holds it past the long-press threshold (500 ms of app time: the clock moves, so the timers run) and lifts it. The element's OnLongPress runs while the finger is down and the press then ends without a click. A touch long press also opens the menu of a kit.ContextMenu or aria.UseContextMenuTrigger (a long press of the mouse does not; see [`App.Click`](#func-app-click) with [`Delay`](#func-delay)). It waits for the element to be visible, enabled, in view and not covered.

```go
app.LongPress(telatest.ByTestID("photo"))
app.ExpectCount(telatest.ByRole("menu", "Actions"), 1)
```

#### func (*App) MainWindow

```go
func (a *App) MainWindow() *App
```

MainWindow returns the App scoped to the app's main window, the one [`Mount`](#func-mount) returned.

#### func (*App) Maximize

```go
func (a *App) Maximize()
```

Maximize maximizes the window to the fake screen ([`Screen`](#func-screen)) as the user does with the OS; it also brings it back from minimized.

#### func (*App) Measure

```go
func (a *App) Measure(f func()) Stats
```

Measure runs f, which performs actions on the app, settles the app afterwards like an action does (with [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), only the work due is handled) and returns the work the tree did meanwhile: the difference of two readings of [`App.Stats`](#func-app-stats), so that a test can assert how narrow an update was without keeping the readings itself. The app is brought to rest before f runs, so work pending from earlier steps is not counted.

```go
st := app.Measure(func() { app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment")) })
if st.Builds != 1 { t.Errorf("the click rebuilt %d components, want 1", st.Builds) }
```

**Example**

```go
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, Counter, telatest.Size(400, 300))

st := app.Measure(func() {
    app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment"))
})
fmt.Println("builds:", st.Builds, "frames:", st.Frames > 0)
// Output: builds: 1 frames: true
```

#### func (*App) MenuBar

```go
func (a *App) MenuBar() []MenuItem
```

MenuBar returns the native menu bar of this App's window (a mounted desktop.MenuBar), nil without one, after settling the app.

#### func (*App) MessageBoxes

```go
func (a *App) MessageBoxes() []MessageBox
```

MessageBoxes returns the message boxes open now, oldest first (native ones before drawn ones), after settling the app.

#### func (*App) Minimize

```go
func (a *App) Minimize()
```

Minimize minimizes the window, as the user does with the OS: it loses the focus and gets no frames until it is restored or activated.

#### func (*App) Modal

```go
func (a *App) Modal() bool
```

Modal reports whether the window is modal to the window it was declared in (tela.Window.Modal).

#### func (*App) MouseDown

```go
func (a *App) MouseDown()
```

MouseDown presses the primary button at the pointer's position (move it first with MouseMove, Hover or Click).

#### func (*App) MouseMove

```go
func (a *App) MouseMove(x, y float32)
```

MouseMove moves the pointer to (x, y), in logical pixels from the window's top-left corner.

#### func (*App) MouseUp

```go
func (a *App) MouseUp()
```

MouseUp releases the primary button.

#### func (*App) MoveWindow

```go
func (a *App) MoveWindow(x, y int)
```

MoveWindow moves the window so that its content area's top-left corner is at (x, y) physical pixels of the fake desktop, as the user dragging it by its title bar (the pointer is [`App.MouseMove`](#func-app-mousemove)'s). The position shows in [`App.Placement`](#func-app-placement) from then on.

#### func (*App) Notifications

```go
func (a *App) Notifications() []Notification
```

Notifications returns the notifications the app showed, oldest first, closed ones included, after settling the app.

#### func (*App) Now

```go
func (a *App) Now() time.Duration
```

Now returns the app's clock: the time since the window was created, as moved by waits and [`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance).

#### func (*App) Parent

```go
func (a *App) Parent() *App
```

Parent returns the window this one was declared in (the App of the window whose component rendered the tela.Window), or nil for the main window.

#### func (*App) PixelAt

```go
func (a *App) PixelAt(x, y float32) color.RGBA
```

PixelAt returns the color of the window's current frame at the point (x, y), in logical pixels from the top-left corner. The frame is in device pixels, so the sampled one is the device pixel that contains the point: (floor(x\*scale), floor(y\*scale)), where scale is the window's display scale; at scale 2, PixelAt(10, 10) reads the pixel (20, 20), the top-left one of the four that cover the logical pixel. The app is settled first (with [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), only the work due is handled). The color is as stored in the frame (alpha-premultiplied; windows are opaque, so A is 255). It fails the test when the point is outside the window.

```go
if c := app.PixelAt(40, 20); c != (color.RGBA{R: 59, G: 130, B: 246, A: 255}) {
    t.Errorf("the button is %v, want blue-500", c)
}
```

**Example**

```go
swatch := func() tela.Node {
    return Div(Class("size-4 bg-[#ff0000]"))
}
// At scale 2 the logical point (8, 8) is the device pixel (16, 16).
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, swatch, telatest.Size(32, 32), telatest.Scale(2))

fmt.Println(app.PixelAt(8, 8), app.PixelAt(20, 20))
// Output: {255 0 0 255} {255 255 255 255}
```

#### func (*App) Placement

```go
func (a *App) Placement() tela.WindowPlacement
```

Placement returns where the window is (tela.WindowHandle.Placement): its size outside maximized and fullscreen, its position once the app or [`App.MoveWindow`](#func-app-movewindow) set one, the state to open in. It still answers after the window closed.

#### func (*App) PopupMenus

```go
func (a *App) PopupMenus() []PopupMenu
```

PopupMenus returns the native context menus open in this App's window, oldest first, after settling the app.

#### func (*App) Press

```go
func (a *App) Press(combo string)
```

Press presses and releases a key, sending the events to the focused element (or, when nothing is focused, to the outermost element of the content). The syntax is Playwright's: a key name or character, with modifiers joined by "+":

```go
app.Press("Enter")
app.Press("Shift+Tab")
app.Press("Control+s")
app.Press("ControlOrMeta+s") // Meta+s under the Mac flavor, Control+s elsewhere
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.Press("a")              // the character "a"
```

Each key is a press and a release with the physical Code, the logical Key, the Text it produces (none for Enter, arrows...), its Location and the modifier state, in the US layout; modifiers are pressed first, as left keys, and released last.

**Example**

```go
search := func() tela.Node {
    query, setQuery := tela.UseState("")
    submitted, setSubmitted := tela.UseState("")
    return Form(OnSubmit(func(tela.SubmitEvent) { setSubmitted.Set(query) }),
        Input(AriaLabel("Search"), Bind(query, setQuery)),
        P(Textf("Searched: %q", submitted)),
    )
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(search))

app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Search"))
app.Type("tela")   // one key at a time
app.Press("Enter") // submits the form
app.ExpectText(`Searched: "tela"`)
fmt.Println("ok")
// Output: ok
```

#### func (*App) PressShortcut

```go
func (a *App) PressShortcut(id string)
```

PressShortcut presses the global shortcut id as the user does, from any application: its OnPress runs and the app settles. It fails the test when no mounted desktop.GlobalShortcut has the ID or it is not bound.

```go
app.PressShortcut("new-note")
app.ExpectText("Untitled note")
```

#### func (*App) RegisteredApps

```go
func (a *App) RegisteredApps() []desktop.HandlerApp
```

RegisteredApps returns the apps registered with desktop.RegisterApp and not unregistered, sorted by ID, after settling the app.

```go
desktop.RegisterApp(desktop.ForApp(desktop.HandlerApp{Exec: "/opt/notes/notes"}))
apps := app.RegisteredApps() // [{com.example.Notes Notes /opt/notes/notes …}]
```

#### func (*App) Registrations

```go
func (a *App) Registrations() []Registration
```

Registrations returns the schemes and file types registered by the app (and by others the test played), sorted by association, after settling the app.

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open notes: links with Notes"))
regs := app.Registrations() // [{notes: {com.example.Notes Notes /path/notes …} viewer true}]
```

#### func (*App) ReleaseShortcut

```go
func (a *App) ReleaseShortcut(id string)
```

ReleaseShortcut releases the global shortcut id (its OnRelease runs), as Linux reports; Windows reports no releases.

#### func (*App) RequestClose

```go
func (a *App) RequestClose()
```

RequestClose asks to close the window as the user does with the close button of its title bar or Alt+F4: the window's OnClose runs (for the main window tela.App.OnClose, or the app quits). Whether the window closes is up to the app: use [`App.ExpectClosed`](#func-app-expectclosed), [`App.ExpectQuit`](#func-app-expectquit) or [`App.ExpectWindowCount`](#func-app-expectwindowcount) to assert it. A blocked window refuses the request and the modal window above it is activated. To press the close button of a custom title bar, click it ([`App.Click`](#func-app-click)).

#### func (*App) RequestQuit

```go
func (a *App) RequestQuit()
```

RequestQuit plays the user or the OS asking the app to quit, as macOS does for Cmd+Q, the app menu's Quit, the Dock's Quit and a logout (tela.App.OnQuit): the app's OnQuit runs ([`OnQuit`](#func-onquit)), or, without one, every window gets a close request as from its close button, so an app whose main window has no OnClose quits. The app settles.

```go
app := telatest.MountApp(t, tela.App{Root: Editor{}, OnQuit: func() { askToSave() }})
app.RequestQuit()
app.ExpectText("Save changes?")
```

#### func (*App) Resize

```go
func (a *App) Resize(width, height float32)
```

Resize changes the logical size of the window, in pixels, as a user resizing it: the app keeps its state, the breakpoint variants (md:, max-lg:) and the layout follow the new size, and the app is settled afterwards (with [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), only the work due is handled). The display scale is kept; [`App.SetScale`](#func-app-setscale) changes it. It fails the test for a size that is not positive. tela mcp's resize tool is built on it (ADR-174).

```go
app.Resize(390, 844) // a phone-sized window
app.ExpectCount(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open menu"), 1)
```

#### func (*App) ResizeStarts

```go
func (a *App) ResizeStarts() []tela.Edge
```

ResizeStarts returns the edges the fake window manager started an interactive resize from, one per primary press on a resize handle (h.WindowResize), in order: the side, or both sides at a corner. The press is the OS's: the app does not see it or the rest of its pointer sequence, and the size does not change by itself (resize the window with [`App.Resize`](#func-app-resize)). A window that cannot be resized (FixedSize, maximized, fullscreen) treats the handles as content.

```go
app.ClickAt(18, 100) // on the left edge of a card 16 px from the window's
if e := app.ResizeStarts(); len(e) != 1 || e[0] != tela.EdgeLeft { … }
```

#### func (*App) Restore

```go
func (a *App) Restore()
```

Restore brings the window back to its normal state: not minimized, not maximized and not fullscreen.

#### func (*App) Screenshot

```go
func (a *App) Screenshot() *image.RGBA
```

Screenshot returns a copy of the window's content, in physical pixels (the logical size times the scale), after settling the app; with [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), the content at the current time, running animations where they are.

#### func (*App) Scroll

```go
func (a *App) Scroll(l Locator, dx, dy float32)
```

Scroll moves the pointer to the center of the element l locates and scrolls the wheel there by (dx, dy) logical pixels, positive to the right and down, as a touchpad does: the nearest scroll container under the pointer that can move scrolls at once, with no animation. Use Press("PageDown") or Press("End") for the animated key scrolling.

#### func (*App) SetAccentColor

```go
func (a *App) SetAccentColor(color tela.Color)
```

SetAccentColor changes the system's accent color (tela.UseAccentColor returns it). Use [`App.ClearAccentColor`](#func-app-clearaccentcolor) for a system without one.

#### func (*App) SetClipboard

```go
func (a *App) SetClipboard(dt *tela.DataTransfer)
```

SetClipboard puts dt's content on the clipboard, as another application copying it would (nil empties it), for the app to paste.

```go
var dt tela.DataTransfer
dt.SetFiles("/home/ana/photo.png")
app.SetClipboard(&dt)
app.Press("Control+V")
```

#### func (*App) SetCompositing

```go
func (a *App) SetCompositing(on bool)
```

SetCompositing plays a compositing manager starting (on) or stopping under a [`Transparent`](#func-transparent) window: the window's [`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate).Transparent follows, it renders opaque while off, and the app settles. It does nothing for other windows.

#### func (*App) SetDarkMode

```go
func (a *App) SetDarkMode(dark bool)
```

SetDarkMode changes whether the system prefers the dark color scheme: the dark: variants apply and tela.UseColorScheme reports it, unless the app sets its own scheme (tela.App.ColorScheme, tela.SetColorScheme, [`ColorScheme`](#func-colorscheme)).

#### func (*App) SetDefaultHandler

```go
func (a *App) SetDefaultHandler(as desktop.Association, holder string)
```

SetDefaultHandler plays the user (or another application) making the application holder the default handler of as; "" removes the explicit default.

#### func (*App) SetFullscreen

```go
func (a *App) SetFullscreen(on bool)
```

SetFullscreen makes the window fullscreen on the fake screen, or leaves fullscreen; entering also brings it back from minimized.

#### func (*App) SetHighContrast

```go
func (a *App) SetHighContrast(high bool)
```

SetHighContrast changes whether the system asks for high contrast: the contrast-more: variants apply and tela.UseHighContrast reports it.

#### func (*App) SetReducedMotion

```go
func (a *App) SetReducedMotion(reduced bool)
```

SetReducedMotion changes whether the system asks for reduced motion: the motion-reduce: variants apply, and transitions that start from now on take no time (tela.UseReducedMotion).

#### func (*App) SetScale

```go
func (a *App) SetScale(scale float64)
```

SetScale moves the window to a display with another scale (device pixels per logical pixel), as a user dragging it between monitors: the logical size and the state are kept and screenshots become width\*scale x height\*scale pixels. The app is settled afterwards (with [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), only the work due is handled). It fails the test for a scale that is not positive. [`App.GoldenScales`](#func-app-goldenscales) compares goldens at several scales without keeping the change.

```go
app.SetScale(2)
```

#### func (*App) SetShortcutStatus

```go
func (a *App) SetShortcutStatus(id string, status desktop.ShortcutStatus, trigger string)
```

SetShortcutStatus plays the OS changing the state of the registered shortcut id: another application took its keys (ShortcutTaken), the user declined it (ShortcutRefused) or removed it (ShortcutRevoked), or bound it to other keys (ShortcutBound with trigger). Its OnStatus runs and the app settles. trigger is ignored unless the status is ShortcutBound; "" then means the keys asked for.

```go
app.SetShortcutStatus("new-note", desktop.ShortcutTaken, "")
app.ExpectText("Ctrl+Alt+N is taken by another application")
```

#### func (*App) SetShortcutUnassigned

```go
func (a *App) SetShortcutUnassigned(id string)
```

SetShortcutUnassigned plays a desktop that registers the shortcut id without assigning it keys, as Hyprland does (the user binds it in hyprland.conf): its OnStatus gets ShortcutBound with an empty Trigger, and the app settles. PressShortcut still works, as once the user bound it.

```go
app.SetShortcutUnassigned("new-note")
app.ExpectText("bind = CTRL ALT, N, global, com.example.notes:new-note")
```

#### func (*App) SetStoredSecret

```go
func (a *App) SetStoredSecret(name string, secret []byte)
```

SetStoredSecret stores a secret under name, as an earlier run of the app would have, before the app reads it with desktop.Secret.

#### func (*App) SetTextScale

```go
func (a *App) SetTextScale(scale float64)
```

SetTextScale changes the system's text scale: 1rem becomes the theme's rem times scale, so type, rem-based spacing and breakpoints change (tela.UseTextScale), unless the app ignores it (tela.App.IgnoreTextScale). scale is above 0 and at most 4; 1 is the default.

#### func (*App) SetTitleBarControls

```go
func (a *App) SetTitleBarControls(r tela.Rect)
```

SetTitleBarControls plays the OS moving or resizing the window buttons it keeps over a [`TitleBarOverlay`](#func-titlebaroverlay) window (macOS places the traffic lights in the height of the app's caption; fullscreen hides them): r is the rectangle in logical window coordinates, and the empty one removes them. The window reports it as [`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate).TitleBarControls, and the app settles. It fails the test for a window that is not a TitleBarOverlay one.

```go
app.SetTitleBarControls(tela.Rect{X: 9, Y: 19, Width: 60, Height: 14})
```

#### func (*App) StartDrag

```go
func (a *App) StartDrag(l Locator) DragInfo
```

StartDrag presses the primary button at the center of the element l locates and moves the pointer away until the app starts a drag, then leaves the drag in progress, owned by the "OS" as a real drag is: the app gets no more pointer events until it ends. Continue it with [`App.HoverDrag`](#func-app-hoverdrag), [`App.DropOn`](#func-app-dropon), [`App.DropOutside`](#func-app-dropoutside), [`App.LeaveDrag`](#func-app-leavedrag) or [`App.CancelDrag`](#func-app-canceldrag). It returns what the drag carries, as [`App.ActiveDrag`](#func-app-activedrag) does.

The element must be h.Draggable(true) and its OnDragStart must put data in e.DataTransfer; an element without data stays an ordinary drag gesture, and StartDrag fails the test.

```go
app.StartDrag(telatest.ByTestID("card-7"))
app.HoverDrag(telatest.ByTestID("column-done"))
app.ExpectText("Release to move here") // the drag-over state of the column
app.DropOn(telatest.ByTestID("column-done"))
```

#### func (*App) Stats

```go
func (a *App) Stats() Stats
```

Stats returns the work counters of the app's tree, after settling it (under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle), handling only the work due).

#### func (*App) StoredSecret

```go
func (a *App) StoredSecret(name string) ([]byte, bool)
```

StoredSecret returns the secret the app stored under name (desktop.SetSecret), and whether there is one. It does not fail while FailSecrets is in effect.

#### func (*App) TakesInput

```go
func (a *App) TakesInput(x, y float32) bool
```

TakesInput reports whether a pointer event at (x, y), logical window coordinates, reaches the app: always, except in a [`Transparent`](#func-transparent) window shown with transparency, where only the pixels of the presented frame whose alpha is at least a quarter take input (the rest goes to what is below the window). It settles the app first.

#### func (*App) Tap

```go
func (a *App) Tap(l Locator)
```

Tap taps the element l locates with a finger: it puts a touch pointer down at the element's center and lifts it, with real touch pointer events (no hover; :active, the gesture arena and the click as for a finger), like Playwright's tap. The element's OnClick runs, with a touch pointer in its event. It waits for the element to be visible, enabled, in view and not covered, and fails the test when l matches none or several.

```go
app.Tap(telatest.ByRole("button", "Save"))
```

#### func (*App) Title

```go
func (a *App) Title() string
```
