Title returns the window's title, as the OS shows it: tela.App.Title or tela.Window.Title, as of the latest build.

#### func (*App) TitleBar

```go
func (a *App) TitleBar() tela.TitleBarColors
```

TitleBar returns the title bar colors the window has asked the OS for (tela.App.TitleBar, tela.Window.TitleBar), at the 8-bit precision the OS takes; a color that is the system's is the zero Color.

#### func (*App) Trashed

```go
func (a *App) Trashed() []string
```

Trashed returns the paths the app moved to the trash with desktop.MoveToTrash, in order, after settling the app. The headless trash moves each into a temporary folder of the test, so the file is gone from its place, as with a real trash; failed calls are not listed.

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Move to Trash"))
app.ExpectText("Moved todo.md to the Trash")
if got := app.Trashed(); len(got) != 1 || got[0] != path {
    t.Errorf("trashed %v", got)
}
```

#### func (*App) Tray

```go
func (a *App) Tray() TrayIcon
```

Tray returns the app's tray icon; it fails the test unless the app shows exactly one.

#### func (*App) Trays

```go
func (a *App) Trays() []TrayIcon
```

Trays returns the tray icons the app shows now, in the order they were added, after settling the app.

#### func (*App) Type

```go
func (a *App) Type(text string)
```

Type types text one character at a time, as key presses and releases sent to the focused element: each has the character's physical Code (US layout, when it has one), Key and Text, and no modifiers (an upper case letter is not typed with Shift, as in Playwright's keyboard.type). A newline types Enter and a tab Tab. In a focused text field each key inserts its text through the real key path (OnKeyDown, then OnBeforeInput and OnChange), as a user typing; [`App.Fill`](#func-app-fill) replaces the value at once.

#### func (*App) Unmaximize

```go
func (a *App) Unmaximize()
```

Unmaximize restores a maximized window to its size.

#### func (*App) Unsupported

```go
func (a *App) Unsupported(services ...DesktopService)
```

Unsupported makes the headless desktop lack the given services from now on, as a desktop without them does (Linux without a portal, GNOME without a tray): the calls return errors wrapping desktop.ErrUnsupported, and ShowMessage draws its box. Called with nothing, every service is supported again.

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, Editor{})
app.Unsupported(telatest.FileDialogs)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open…"))
app.ExpectText("Type the path of the file")
```

#### func (*App) WaitFor

```go
func (a *App) WaitFor(what string, cond func() bool)
```

WaitFor waits until cond reports true, settling the app and letting a frame of app time and a moment of real time pass between tries, until the timeout (see [`Timeout`](#func-timeout)); under [`NoSettle`](#func-nosettle) the first try handles only the work due, and the clock moves only between failed tries. It is for conditions the locators cannot see: a value computed from [`App.Bounds`](#func-app-bounds), or Go state that a goroutine sets. what names the condition in the failure message ("the progress bar reached 3 s"). cond runs on the test goroutine.

#### func (*App) WaitForWindow

```go
func (a *App) WaitForWindow(open func()) *App
```

WaitForWindow runs open, which should make the app open a window (a click, a key press, a goroutine started by one), and returns the App of the window that opened as a result, waiting for it: Playwright's page.waitForEvent('popup'). When several windows opened it returns the first of them. It fails the test at the timeout.

```go
settings := app.WaitForWindow(func() {
    app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Settings"))
})
settings.ExpectText("Preferences")
```

**Example**

```go
var clicks int
var cleaned []string
app := mountNotes(t, &clicks, &cleaned)

settings := app.WaitForWindow(func() {
    app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Settings"))
})
settings.ExpectText("Preferences")
settings.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Applied 0"))
settings.ExpectText("Applied 1")
fmt.Println(settings.Title(), settings.Modal(), app.Blocked(), len(app.Windows()))
// Output: Settings true true 2
```

#### func (*App) Window

```go
func (a *App) Window(title string) *App
```

Window returns the open window whose title is title (exactly), waiting until there is one, as Playwright waits for a locator. It fails the test at the timeout, listing the titles of the open windows, and at once when several windows have the title (select one with [`App.WindowAt`](#func-app-windowat)).

```go
settings := app.Window("Settings")
settings.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Close"))
```

#### func (*App) WindowAt

```go
func (a *App) WindowAt(i int) *App
```

WindowAt returns the open window at index i in the order the windows opened (0 is the main window), waiting until there are that many.

#### func (*App) WindowMenus

```go
func (a *App) WindowMenus() int
```

WindowMenus returns how many secondary presses in a caption region opened the window menu of the fake window manager.

#### func (*App) WindowSize

```go
func (a *App) WindowSize() (width, height float32)
```

WindowSize returns the size of the window's content area in logical pixels, as the app was told (a maximized window has the fake screen's size, see [`Screen`](#func-screen)).

#### func (*App) WindowState

```go
func (a *App) WindowState() tela.WindowState
```

WindowState returns the window's state as the app sees it (tela.WindowHandle.State): maximized, fullscreen and minimized as the fake window manager reported them, whether the window is the active one, whether the app hid it, and whether the app draws its title bar.

#### func (*App) Windows

```go
func (a *App) Windows() []*App
```

Windows returns the app's open windows in the order they opened, the main window first: an [`App`](#type-app) scoped to each, with the same queries, actions, expectations and goldens as the one Mount returns. A window that is hidden (the app's Hidden, a hidden Window) or minimized is still open and listed. The app is settled first, so a window a handler just asked for is listed; use [`App.WaitForWindow`](#func-app-waitforwindow) or [`App.ExpectWindowCount`](#func-app-expectwindowcount) for one that opens later (a goroutine, a timer). Like Playwright's context.pages().

```go
for _, w := range app.Windows() {
    t.Logf("%q is %v", w.Title(), w.WindowState())
}
```

### type ClickOption

```go
type ClickOption func(*clickConfig)
```

ClickOption configures [`App.Click`](#func-app-click) and [`App.ClickAt`](#func-app-clickat).

#### func Delay

```go
func Delay(d time.Duration) ClickOption
```

Delay holds the button down for d of app time between the press and the release, like Playwright's click delay. It is how a test makes a long press of the mouse (the arena recognizes one after 500 ms): the handler runs while the button is held and the release then ends the press without a click. For a touch long press, which opens a context menu, use [`App.LongPress`](#func-app-longpress).

#### func Right

```go
func Right() ClickOption
```

Right makes [`App.Click`](#func-app-click) and [`App.ClickAt`](#func-app-clickat) press and release the secondary (right) mouse button, like Playwright's click({button: 'right'}): real pointer events with the secondary button, so the element's OnContextMenu runs once the button is released (a kit.ContextMenu opens) and its OnClick does not. The element must be as actionable as for a primary click: visible, enabled, in view and not covered. It combines with [`Delay`](#func-delay).

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByTestID("area"), telatest.Right())
app.ClickAt(120, 80, telatest.Right())
```

### type DesktopService

```go
type DesktopService uint8
```

DesktopService is a group of desktop services, for [`App.Unsupported`](#func-app-unsupported).

```go
const (
    // FileDialogs: desktop.OpenFile, OpenFiles, SaveFile, PickFolder.
    FileDialogs DesktopService = iota + 1
    // MessageBoxes: the native message box of desktop.ShowMessage; without
    // it the box is drawn in a window, as on Linux.
    MessageBoxes
    // Notifications: desktop.Notify.
    Notifications
    // TrayIcons: desktop.Tray.
    TrayIcons
    // OpenURLs: tela.OpenURL and tela.OpenPath.
    OpenURLs
    // NativeMenus: desktop.PopupMenu and desktop.MenuBar, as on Linux
    // (the app draws its menus instead).
    NativeMenus
    // GlobalShortcuts: desktop.GlobalShortcut (OnStatus gets
    // ShortcutFailed), as on Wayland without the portal.
    GlobalShortcuts
    // Secrets: desktop.SetSecret, Secret and DeleteSecret, as on a Linux
    // session without a keyring.
    Secrets
    // ClipboardData: desktop.ReadClipboard, WriteClipboard and
    // ClipboardTypes (the text functions keep working).
    ClipboardData
    // Associations: desktop.Register, Unregister, MakeDefault,
    // RegistrationStatus, RegisterApp, UnregisterApp and AppStatus while
    // the app runs, as on macOS before its desktop integration.
    Associations
    // Trash: desktop.MoveToTrash, as on a desktop without a trash or for
    // a file the trash cannot take (a network drive); the file stays.
    Trash
    // AppMenu: desktop.AppMenuBar's platform bar, which only macOS has
    // (the headless desktop has it unless this takes it away): without it
    // the app's bar becomes the bar of every framed window, as on Windows
    // (with NativeMenus unsupported too, as on Linux, nothing is native
    // and the app draws it).
    AppMenu
)
```

### type DragInfo

```go
type DragInfo struct {
    // Data is a copy of what the drag carries, with every getter open
    // (Types, Text, HTML, Files, Image, GetData...). Its EffectAllowed is
    // Allowed.
    Data *tela.DataTransfer
    // Allowed are the effects the source allows.
    Allowed tela.DropEffect
    // External: another application's drag. Source is the window of the
    // app that started it, nil for an external drag.
    External bool
    Source   *App
    // Over is the window the drag is over, nil while it is over none.
    Over *App
}
```

DragInfo describes the drag in progress ([`App.ActiveDrag`](#func-app-activedrag)).

### type DragOption

```go
type DragOption func(*dragConfig)
```

DragOption configures [`App.Drag`](#func-app-drag), [`App.DragBy`](#func-app-dragby) and [`App.DragFromTo`](#func-app-dragfromto).

#### func Allowed

```go
func Allowed(effects ...tela.DropEffect) DragOption
```

Allowed sets the effects the other application allows for the drag that [`Carrying`](#func-carrying) starts (default: copy, move and link). The app's DataTransfer.EffectAllowed in its handlers reports them, and a drop refuses an effect outside them.

#### func Carrying

```go
func Carrying(payload DragPayload) DragOption
```

Carrying makes the step start another application's drag of payload when no drag is in progress, instead of failing. [`App.HoverDrag`](#func-app-hoverdrag) and [`App.DropOn`](#func-app-dropon) take it; [`App.DropData`](#func-app-dropdata) and [`App.DropFiles`](#func-app-dropfiles) are DropOn with it.

#### func Modifiers

```go
func Modifiers(keys ...string) DragOption
```

Modifiers holds keys during the step, with Playwright's names ("Shift", "Control", "Alt", "Meta", "ControlOrMeta"). The platform's convention picks the default DropEffect from them: Control copies, Shift moves, Control+Shift links.

#### func Steps

```go
func Steps(n int) DragOption
```

Steps sets how many pointer moves the drag is made of (default 12): the pointer moves in equal steps between the start and the end, and each move runs a frame, as a window would.

### type DragPayload

```go
type DragPayload struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

DragPayload is the data another application drags: files, text, HTML, a PNG image or a custom type, in one or more representations. Build it with [`DragFiles`](#func-dragfiles), [`DragText`](#func-dragtext), [`DragHTML`](#func-draghtml), [`DragPNG`](#func-dragpng) and [`DragType`](#func-dragtype), and combine representations, best first, with [`DragPayload.And`](#func-dragpayload-and).

#### func DragFiles

```go
func DragFiles(paths ...string) DragPayload
```

DragFiles is a list of files, as a file manager drags them: the app reads their paths with DataTransfer.Files. The paths must be absolute (use t.TempDir()); the files need not exist.

#### func DragHTML

```go
func DragHTML(html string) DragPayload
```

DragHTML is an HTML fragment (the "text/html" type). Add [`DragText`](#func-dragtext) with [`DragPayload.And`](#func-dragpayload-and) for applications that read only text.

#### func DragPNG

```go
func DragPNG(img image.Image) DragPayload
```

DragPNG is an image, carried as "image/png".

#### func DragText

```go
func DragText(s string) DragPayload
```

DragText is plain text (the "text/plain" type).

#### func DragType

```go
func DragType(mime string, data string) DragPayload
```

DragType is data of a custom MIME type, such as "application/x-card" (HTML's setData). It panics when mime is not a MIME type.

#### func (DragPayload) And

```go
func (p DragPayload) And(other DragPayload) DragPayload
```

And returns the payload with the representations of other added after its own. It panics when both carry the same type.

```go
telatest.DragHTML("<b>Hi</b>").And(telatest.DragText("Hi"))
```

### type FileDialog

```go
type FileDialog struct {
    Kind FileDialogKind
    // Title, Directory and DefaultName are the options the app gave
    // (desktop.Title, Directory, DefaultName).
    Title, Directory, DefaultName string
    // Filters are the desktop.Filter entries.
    Filters []desktop.FileFilter
}
```

FileDialog is a file dialog the app opened and the test has not answered.

### type FileDialogKind

```go
type FileDialogKind string
```

FileDialogKind is the kind of a [`FileDialog`](#type-filedialog).

```go
const (
    OpenFileDialog   FileDialogKind = "OpenFile"   // desktop.OpenFile
    OpenFilesDialog  FileDialogKind = "OpenFiles"  // desktop.OpenFiles (several files)
    SaveFileDialog   FileDialogKind = "SaveFile"   // desktop.SaveFile
    PickFolderDialog FileDialogKind = "PickFolder" // desktop.PickFolder
)
```

### type FilterOption

```go
type FilterOption func(*Locator)
```

FilterOption narrows a locator in [`Locator.Filter`](#func-locator-filter).

#### func HasClass

```go
func HasClass(classes ...string) FilterOption
```

HasClass keeps the elements that have all the given Tailwind class names. Like [`ByClass`](#func-byclass) it ties the test to the styling.

#### func HasText

```go
func HasText(text string) FilterOption
```

HasText keeps the elements whose text content contains text (a case-insensitive substring, whitespace normalized), like Playwright's filter({hasText}).

### type GlobalShortcut

```go
type GlobalShortcut struct {
    ID, Description string
    // Keys is the combination asked for, written the usual way
    // ("Ctrl+Alt+N").
    Keys string
    // Status and Trigger are the latest outcome the app was told
    // (ShortcutStatusEvent).
    Status  desktop.ShortcutStatus
    Trigger string
}
```

GlobalShortcut is a global shortcut the app registered (a mounted desktop.GlobalShortcut).

### type GoldenOption

```go
type GoldenOption struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

GoldenOption configures [`App.Golden`](#func-app-golden).

#### func Tolerance

```go
func Tolerance(maxDelta uint8, maxPixels int) GoldenOption
```

Tolerance lets a golden comparison accept small differences: pixels whose channels differ by at most maxDelta (0 to 255, on premultiplied values) count as equal, and up to maxPixels pixels may differ by more. Without it a golden must match bit by bit: Tela's pixels are the same on every platform (ADR-027), so only a deliberate change should alter one.

### type HitKind

```go
type HitKind = platform.HitKind
```

HitKind is what a region of a window's custom title bar is to the OS.

`HitKind` is an alias of `platform.HitKind`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type HitKind uint8
```

```go
const (
    // HitClient is ordinary content. It is what lies outside every
    // region, and a HitClient region punches a hole into the regions
    // listed before it (a search field or a tab strip inside a caption
    // area).
    HitClient HitKind = iota
    // HitCaption is a drag area of the title bar: the OS handles presses
    // in it (move, double-click, window menu).
    HitCaption
    // HitMinimize, HitMaximize and HitClose are the window buttons drawn
    // by the app. Pointer events over them reach the app as usual (its
    // buttons perform the action); the region tells the OS what they are
    // (Windows 11 snap layouts open from the maximize button).
    HitMinimize
    HitMaximize
    HitClose
    // HitResizeTop to HitResizeBottomRight are resize handles the app
    // marks along its content's edges (h.WindowResize, contract v10,
    // ADR-257): a press there is the OS's and starts an interactive
    // resize from that side or corner, and the backend shows its resize
    // cursor ([Edge.Cursor]), as over the backends' own band. Where the
    // window cannot be resized (FixedSize, maximized, fullscreen) they
    // are content. [KindEdge] gives a kind's edge, [HitResize] the kind
    // of an edge.
    HitResizeTop
    HitResizeBottom
    HitResizeLeft
    HitResizeRight
    HitResizeTopLeft
    HitResizeTopRight
    HitResizeBottomLeft
    HitResizeBottomRight
)
```

#### func (HitKind) String

```go
func (k HitKind) String() string
```

### type HitRegion

```go
type HitRegion struct {
    Kind HitKind
    Rect tela.Rect
}
```

HitRegion is one rectangle of a window's custom title bar, in logical pixels from the window's top-left corner.

#### func (HitRegion) String

```go
func (r HitRegion) String() string
```

### type Locator

```go
type Locator struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Locator describes the element an action or expectation works on, like a Playwright locator: it is resolved against the live semantics tree each time it is used, so it keeps working when the app rebuilds. Make one with [`ByRole`](#func-byrole), [`ByText`](#func-bytext), [`ByClass`](#func-byclass) or [`ByTestID`](#func-bytestid) and narrow it with [`Locator.Filter`](#func-locator-filter) and [`Locator.Nth`](#func-locator-nth).

Hidden elements (display: none, visibility other than visible, AriaHidden, and their descendants) are never matched. An action needs the locator to match exactly one element (strictness, as in Playwright) and fails with the aria snapshot and the closest names when it matches none or several.

#### func ByClass

```go
func ByClass(classes ...string) Locator
```

ByClass locates the elements that have all the given Tailwind class names. It is an escape hatch for elements without a role or text, and ties the test to the styling: prefer [`ByRole`](#func-byrole) and [`ByText`](#func-bytext). It matches an h.Icon that has no name (decorative, hidden from accessibility) as well as the visible elements; other hidden elements are not matched.

```go
telatest.ByClass("rounded-full", "shadow-sm")
```

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println(telatest.ByClass("rounded-full", "shadow-sm"))
// Output: getByClass("rounded-full shadow-sm")
```

#### func ByRole

```go
func ByRole(role, name string) Locator
```

ByRole locates the elements with an ARIA role (explicit with h.Role or implicit: button, heading, link, checkbox...) and, when name is not empty, exactly this accessible name (whitespace normalized, case sensitive). Elements without a role of their own (Div, Span) are never matched by role, as in Playwright. An empty name matches any name.

```go
telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment")
telatest.ByRole("heading", "")
```

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println(telatest.ByRole("button", "Increment"))
fmt.Println(telatest.ByRole("heading", ""))
// Output:
// getByRole("button", name="Increment")
// getByRole("heading")
```

#### func ByTestID

```go
func ByTestID(id string) Locator
```

ByTestID locates the element that carries the h.TestID with this exact id, like Playwright's getByTestId. It is the way to find an element a user cannot name (a card, a chart, a drop zone); the id is not part of the semantics tree or the aria snapshot, so it is never visible to assistive technologies. Hidden elements are not matched, like with the other locators, except a decorative h.Icon.

```go
telatest.ByTestID("sidebar")
```

**Example**

```go
card := func() tela.Node {
    return Div(TestID("card"), Class("size-16 bg-slate-200"))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, card, telatest.Size(100, 100))

fmt.Println(telatest.ByTestID("card"))
fmt.Println(app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("card")))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot() == "") // the id is not in the snapshot
// Output:
// getByTestId("card")
// {0 0 64 64}
// true
```

#### func ByText

```go
func ByText(text string, opts ...TextOption) Locator
```

ByText locates the elements that contain text, like Playwright's getByText: it matches the text content of an element (whitespace normalized, hidden descendants left out, block boundaries counting as spaces) and picks the deepest elements that match, so the button that holds the text rather than the page that holds the button. The match is a case-insensitive substring unless [`Exact`](#func-exact) is given.

```go
telatest.ByText("Count: 1")
telatest.ByText("Save", telatest.Exact())
```

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println(telatest.ByText("Count"))
fmt.Println(telatest.ByText("Save", telatest.Exact()))
// Output:
// getByText("Count")
// getByText("Save", exact)
```

#### func (Locator) Filter

```go
func (l Locator) Filter(opts ...FilterOption) Locator
```

Filter returns a locator that matches only the elements of l that satisfy the options.

```go
telatest.ByRole("button", "").Filter(telatest.HasText("System"))
```

**Example**

```go
rows := telatest.ByRole("button", "").Filter(telatest.HasText("System"))
fmt.Println(rows)
// Output: getByRole("button").filter(hasText="System")
```

#### func (Locator) Nth

```go
func (l Locator) Nth(i int) Locator
```

Nth returns a locator for the i-th match of l (0 is the first; a negative i counts from the end, so -1 is the last). It turns a locator that matches several elements into one that matches one.

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println(telatest.ByRole("listitem", "").Nth(0))
fmt.Println(telatest.ByRole("listitem", "").Nth(-1)) // the last one
// Output:
// getByRole("listitem").nth(0)
// getByRole("listitem").nth(-1)
```

#### func (Locator) String

```go
func (l Locator) String() string
```

String describes the locator the way Playwright does.

### type MenuItem

```go
type MenuItem struct {
    Label, Accelerator           string
    Separator, Checkbox, Checked bool
    Disabled                     bool
    // Role is the item's (or submenu's) role, as the app gave it
    // (desktop.MenuItem.Role).
    Role    desktop.Role
    Submenu []MenuItem
}
```

MenuItem is an item of a native menu: a popup menu (desktop.PopupMenu), a window's menu bar (desktop.MenuBar) or the app's (desktop.AppMenuBar).

### type MessageBox

```go
type MessageBox struct {
    Kind    desktop.MessageKind
    Title   string
    Text    string
    Buttons desktop.Buttons
    // Drawn: Tela draws the box in a window (the desktop has no native
    // message box, as on Linux; see [App.Unsupported]).
    Drawn bool
}
```

MessageBox is a message box the app shows (desktop.ShowMessage) and the test has not answered.

### type Notification

```go
type Notification struct {
    Title, Body string
    // Actions are the labels of its buttons.
    Actions []string
    // Closed: the app closed it, or the user clicked or dismissed it.
    Closed bool
}
```

Notification is a notification the app showed (desktop.Notify).

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*config)
```

Option configures [`Mount`](#func-mount) and the headless entry points [`Render`](#func-render), [`AriaSnapshot`](#func-ariasnapshot) and [`LayoutJSON`](#func-layoutjson).

#### func AccentColor

```go
func AccentColor(color tela.Color) Option
```

AccentColor sets the system's accent color, which tela.UseAccentColor returns (by default the system has none).

#### func AllowDev

```go
func AllowDev(substrings ...string) Option
```

AllowDev lists dev errors that do not fail a test: those containing any of the substrings, which are logged instead. Dev warnings never fail a test, and AllowDev does nothing under [`NoDev`](#func-nodev).

#### func AlwaysOnTop

```go
func AlwaysOnTop() Option
```

AlwaysOnTop keeps the main window above the others (tela.App.AlwaysOnTop).

#### func AppID

```go
func AppID(id string) Option
```

AppID sets the application identity the window reports to the desktop (tela.App.AppID).

#### func Backdrop

```go
func Backdrop(b tela.Backdrop) Option
```

Backdrop sets the system backdrop of the main window (tela.App.Backdrop). The fake window manager only records it: [`App.Backdrop`](#func-app-backdrop) reads it back.

#### func CheckDamage

```go
func CheckDamage() Option
```

CheckDamage makes the app compare its window with a full rendering after every frame (when nothing is left to draw), and fail the test on the first pixel that differs: frames are rasterized incrementally (only what changed, scrolled content shifted), and must give the pixels a full rasterization gives. It makes every frame cost a full rendering; it is for tests of rendering, and TELA_CHECK_DAMAGE=1 turns it on everywhere.

#### func ClassAliases

```go
func ClassAliases(aliases map[string]string) Option
```

ClassAliases sets the app's class aliases, like tela.App.ClassAliases: class names that expand to class strings where they appear.

#### func ClassicScrollbars

```go
func ClassicScrollbars() Option
```

ClassicScrollbars draws always-visible classic scrollbars that take space (tela.App.ClassicScrollbars).

#### func ColorScheme

```go
func ColorScheme(s tela.ColorScheme) Option
```

ColorScheme sets the app's color scheme, like tela.App.ColorScheme: tela.Light or tela.Dark override the system's preference ([`Dark`](#func-dark) sets that one), tela.System follows it. tela.SetColorScheme changes it while the app runs.

**Example**

```go
swatch := Div(Class("size-8 bg-white dark:bg-black"))
light, _ := telatest.Render(swatch, telatest.Size(8, 8), telatest.Dark(), telatest.ColorScheme(tela.Light))
dark, _ := telatest.Render(swatch, telatest.Size(8, 8), telatest.ColorScheme(tela.Dark))
fmt.Println(light.RGBAAt(4, 4), dark.RGBAAt(4, 4))
// Output: {255 255 255 255} {0 0 0 255}
```

#### func Dark

```go
func Dark() Option
```

Dark makes the system prefer the dark color scheme, so the dark: variants apply unless the app sets another scheme ([`ColorScheme`](#func-colorscheme), tela.App.ColorScheme, tela.SetColorScheme).

#### func Debug

```go
func Debug(flags ...string) Option
```

Debug turns debug overlays on: any of "layout", "paint-flash", "layers", "fps" and "semantics" (or "all"), the values TELA_DEBUG takes. The overlays are drawn over the window, so [`App.Screenshot`](#func-app-screenshot) and [`App.Golden`](#func-app-golden) show them; the headless entry points ([`Render`](#func-render)) draw them too. TELA_DEBUG itself is ignored, so goldens never depend on the environment. An unknown name fails the test with the valid ones.

A paint flash fades over 300 ms of app time, and the fps meter redraws on every frame; neither keeps an action waiting (they are not work the app must finish), so look at them with [`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance). See [`DebugClock`](#func-debugclock) for the frame times the meter shows.

#### func DebugClock

```go
func DebugClock(now func() time.Duration) Option
```

DebugClock replaces the clock the fps overlay times frames with: a frame took the difference between two readings of now, taken before and after it. The default reads 1 ms longer at every call, so every frame takes 1 ms and goldens do not depend on the machine; tests of the meter pass a scripted clock.

#### func Dev

```go
func Dev() Option
```

Dev turns dev mode on. It is the default since dev mode became the default (see [`NoDev`](#func-nodev)), so Dev changes nothing; it is kept for the tests written before, and undoes a [`NoDev`](#func-nodev) given earlier in the options.

#### func FixedSize

```go
func FixedSize() Option
```

FixedSize keeps the user from resizing the main window (tela.App.FixedSize).

#### func Fonts

```go
func Fonts(fonts ...tela.Font) Option
```

Fonts adds fonts to the app, before the deterministic set every app has (the fonts of fonts/standard: Inter, JetBrains Mono, Source Serif 4, Noto Sans Arabic and Noto Color Emoji), like tela.App.Fonts: they win the generic families they stand for (a Sans() font replaces Inter as font-sans) and are tried first in fallback. Tests never use the system's fonts, so goldens are the same on every machine. A font that cannot be used (a FontFS pattern that matches nothing, a file that is not a font) fails the test at Mount.

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, Notes(), telatest.Fonts(tela.FontData("Lora", lora).Serif()))
```

#### func Frameless

```go
func Frameless() Option
```

Frameless gives the main window no OS title bar (tela.App.Frameless): its [`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate) reports ClientSideDecorations, and the content draws its own title bar with h.WindowDrag and h.WindowControl.

#### func FromApp

```go
func FromApp(app tela.App) Option
```

FromApp applies the settings of a [`tela.App`](API-Reference-tela#type-app) that shape what is drawn, so a test, `tela snapshot` and the window see the same app: the size when both Width and Height are set, RootClass, ColorScheme, Theme, ClassAliases, Fonts, ClassicScrollbars, InstantScroll, NativeMenus, IgnoreTextScale, Dev and Transparent (the picture keeps the frame's alpha, as [`Transparent`](#func-transparent)). It sets only what the app sets, so it never undoes an earlier option, and the options after it override it:

```go
var App = tela.App{Title: "Notes", Width: 900, Height: 600, RootClass: "bg-background", Root: Notes()}

app := telatest.Mount(t, Notes(), telatest.FromApp(App))
app := telatest.Mount(t, Notes{}, telatest.FromApp(App), telatest.Size(400, 300))
```

Title, AppID, Root, DevState and the fields of the OS window (size limits, FixedSize, Frameless, AlwaysOnTop, Hidden, Icon, Placement, OnClose) say nothing about how the content looks, so FromApp ignores them: tools that only render the app (`tela snapshot`, `tela mcp`) want it visible and quit-able whatever the app does with its window. [`MountApp`](#func-mountapp) mounts Root and applies those fields too, as the options [`Title`](#func-title), [`MinSize`](#func-minsize), [`Frameless`](#func-frameless), [`StartHidden`](#func-starthidden), [`Placement`](#func-placement), [`OnClose`](#func-onclose) and the others do by hand. The scale is not an App setting (it comes from the display): use [`Scale`](#func-scale).

**Example**

```go
appSettings := tela.App{Width: 400, Height: 300, RootClass: "bg-slate-100"}
// Mount a struct component (or a tela.Preview) in the app's window.
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(Counter), telatest.FromApp(appSettings), telatest.Scale(2))

fmt.Println(app.Screenshot().Bounds().Size())
// Output: (800,600)
```

#### func HighContrast

```go
func HighContrast() Option
```

HighContrast makes the system ask for high contrast: the contrast-more: variants apply and tela.UseHighContrast reports true.

#### func Icon

```go
func Icon(images ...image.Image) Option
```

Icon sets the icon of the main window (tela.App.Icon): the same picture at several sizes.

#### func InstantScroll

```go
func InstantScroll() Option
```

InstantScroll makes user scrolling jump, without animation or flings (tela.App.InstantScroll).

#### func MaxSize

```go
func MaxSize(width, height float32) Option
```

MaxSize limits the size of the main window from above; see [`MinSize`](#func-minsize).

#### func MinSize

```go
func MinSize(width, height float32) Option
```

MinSize and MaxSize limit the size the user can give the main window (tela.App.MinWidth and MinHeight, MaxWidth and MaxHeight); zero is no limit on that side. The fake window manager clamps [`App.Resize`](#func-app-resize), maximizing and fullscreen to them.

#### func Monitors

```go
func Monitors(workAreas ...image.Rectangle) Option
```

Monitors gives the fake desktop monitors whose work areas (the monitor without its task bar) are the given rectangles, the primary first, in physical pixels of the desktop: the space of [`App.MoveWindow`](#func-app-movewindow) and of [`tela.WindowPlacement`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowplacement) X and Y. A window that opens at a position where it could not be grabbed on any of them (a placement saved while another monitor was connected) opens on the nearest one instead, as on Windows, macOS and X11, and [`App.Placement`](#func-app-placement) reports where it went:

```go
saved := tela.WindowPlacement{Width: 800, Height: 600, X: 2500, Y: 100, HasPosition: true}
app := telatest.MountApp(t, tela.App{Placement: saved, Root: Notes{}},
    telatest.Monitors(image.Rect(0, 0, 1920, 1040))) // the second monitor is gone
// app.Placement() is at 1120,100: on the laptop's screen
```

Without it no monitors are known and windows open where they are asked to. Moves after a window opens ([`App.MoveWindow`](#func-app-movewindow), tela.WindowHandle SetPosition) are never changed.

#### func NoCompositing

```go
func NoCompositing() Option
```

NoCompositing plays a desktop that cannot show transparency, as X11 without a compositing manager: a [`Transparent`](#func-transparent) window is an opaque frameless one, its [`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate).Transparent is false and it takes input everywhere. [`App.SetCompositing`](#func-app-setcompositing) changes it while the app runs.

#### func NoDev

```go
func NoDev() Option
```

NoDev turns dev mode off. Apps and the headless entry points run in dev mode by default, as a development build of an app does: unknown classes, roles, input types and easings, hooks called in another order or outside their component, and the dev warnings (lists without keys, nil dependencies, a Value read while changes are queued, a Label without a control...) are reported. With [`Mount`](#func-mount), a dev error (an unknown class, an image that cannot be loaded) fails the test at the action that caused it unless [`AllowDev`](#func-allowdev) lists it, a dev panic fails it as any panic does, and a warning is a test log line; with [`Render`](#func-render) and the other entry points, errors and warnings go to standard error.

Use NoDev to test what a release build does. The checks of the node constructors (h.If with a struct component, Role, Type, Dir...) follow the app's dev mode when they run while a component builds, as in a function given to [`MountFunc`](#func-mountfunc); a node built outside any build (the root passed to [`Mount`](#func-mount) in the test's body) follows the process default, which is on in a test binary. TELA_DEV=1 or TELA_DEV=0 in the environment overrides both NoDev and the default.

**Example**

```go
// A typo in a class: in dev mode (the default) it fails the test with
// the closest class, "rounded-2xl".
card := func() tela.Node { return Div(Class("rounded-xxl p-4"), Text("Card")) }

// NoDev tests what a release build does: the class is ignored and the
// test goes on.
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(card), telatest.Size(200, 100), telatest.NoDev())
app.ExpectText("Card")
fmt.Println("ok")
// Output: ok
```

#### func NoServerDecorations

```go
func NoServerDecorations() Option
```

NoServerDecorations makes the fake window manager draw no title bars, as GNOME on Wayland does: every window, framed or not, reports ClientSideDecorations, so a test can check that the app draws its own bar (kit.TitleBar) there. A framed window without an h.WindowDrag area of its own then shows Tela's fallback title bar (see tela.App), with its window buttons, and its content below it.

#### func NoSettle

```go
func NoSettle() Option
```

NoSettle makes the app keep its animations where they are for [`App.Screenshot`](#func-app-screenshot) and [`App.Golden`](#func-app-golden), so a test can capture the frames of a transition, a [`tela.UseSpring`](API-Reference-tela#func-usespring) or the enter and exit of an h.Presence:

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, Dialog(), telatest.NoSettle())
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open"))
app.Advance(100 * time.Millisecond)
app.Golden("dialog_100ms.png") // 100 ms into the entrance
```

With it, Mount, the events of an action, Screenshot and Golden and the queries [`App.AriaSnapshot`](#func-app-ariasnapshot), [`App.Count`](#func-app-count), [`App.Bounds`](#func-app-bounds), [`App.Stats`](#func-app-stats) and [`App.Cursor`](#func-app-cursor) handle the work due (state updates, the frames they ask for) but do not run the clock until running transitions and animations end: the clock moves with [`App.Advance`](#func-app-advance). The expectations poll as ever, but their first try handles only the work due, and the clock moves a frame at a time only between failed tries. What keeps its full auto-wait is the wait before an action: before acting, an action waits for the app to settle (so the animations an earlier step started end first).

**Example**

```go
// A box that fades in over 200 ms when it is shown.
page := func() tela.Node {
    shown, setShown := tela.UseState(false)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setShown.Set(true) }), Text("Show")),
        If(shown, Div(Class("size-10 bg-black transition-opacity duration-200 ease-linear starting:opacity-0"))))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(page), telatest.Size(100, 100), telatest.NoSettle())
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Show"))
app.Advance(100 * time.Millisecond)
// Halfway: black at 50% over white. app.Golden("fade_100ms.png") would
// capture the same frame.
fmt.Println(app.Screenshot().RGBAAt(5, 40))
app.Advance(100 * time.Millisecond)
fmt.Println(app.Screenshot().RGBAAt(5, 40))
// Output:
// {128 128 128 255}
// {0 0 0 255}
```

#### func OnClose

```go
func OnClose(f func(tela.WindowHandle)) Option
```

OnClose sets what closing the main window does (tela.App.OnClose): f runs when the user asks to close it ([`App.RequestClose`](#func-app-requestclose), a WindowClose control, WindowHandle.Close). Without it the app quits.

#### func OnQuit

```go
func OnQuit(f func()) Option
```

OnQuit sets what a request to quit does (tela.App.OnQuit): f runs when the user or the OS asks the app to quit ([`App.RequestQuit`](#func-app-requestquit); macOS's Cmd+Q and the Dock's Quit). Without it every window gets a close request.

#### func Placement

```go
func Placement(p tela.WindowPlacement) Option
```

Placement opens the main window where a previous run left it (tela.App.Placement): a [`tela.WindowPlacement`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowplacement) saved from tela.WindowHandle.Placement or [`App.Placement`](#func-app-placement). Its size, when set, wins over [`Size`](#func-size).

#### func PlatformKeys

```go
func PlatformKeys(goos string) Option
```

PlatformKeys makes the app follow the key conventions of the platform goos names, a runtime.GOOS value: "darwin" for macOS, "windows" for Windows, anything else for Linux (ADR-221). The key bindings and word rules of text fields follow it (Command+A selects all, Option+Left moves by word under "darwin"), and so do the events' CmdOrCtrl and the aria hooks built on it (Command+click toggles a selection on a Mac), and [`App.Press`](#func-app-press) and [`Modifiers`](#func-modifiers) resolve "ControlOrMeta" to Meta under "darwin" and to Control otherwise. Without it the app follows the OS the test runs on. It applies to one app and its windows, so parallel tests with different platforms do not interfere:

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, Editor(), telatest.PlatformKeys("darwin"))
app.Press("ControlOrMeta+a") // Meta+a: selects all
app.Press("Alt+ArrowLeft")   // Option+Left: one word back
```

Only the conventions change: the headless backend, the look of the app and what the app reads from runtime.GOOS stay those of the host.

#### func PreferNativeMenus

```go
func PreferNativeMenus() Option
```

PreferNativeMenus makes kit's ContextMenu and Menubar use the OS's menus where the platform has them (tela.App.NativeMenus, ADR-215). The headless desktop has them, unless [`App.Unsupported`](#func-app-unsupported) takes them away ([`NativeMenus`](#type-desktopservice)) or the window is [`Frameless`](#func-frameless) (no menu bar). Answer a native context menu with [`App.ChoosePopupItem`](#func-app-choosepopupitem) and read a native bar with [`App.MenuBar`](#func-app-menubar).

#### func ReducedMotion

```go
func ReducedMotion() Option
```

ReducedMotion makes the system ask for reduced motion: the motion-reduce: variants apply, transitions take no time and scrolling jumps.

#### func RootClass

```go
func RootClass(classes string) Option
```

RootClass sets the classes of the root box, which fills the window (tela.App.RootClass): a background, a text style, overflow-hidden.

#### func Scale

```go
func Scale(scale float64) Option
```

Scale sets the display scale: device pixels per logical pixel (default 1). Screenshots and goldens are (width\*scale) x (height\*scale) pixels.

#### func Screen

```go
func Screen(width, height float32) Option
```

Screen sets the logical size of the fake screen: what maximized and fullscreen windows grow to (default 1920 by 1080).

#### func Size

```go
func Size(width, height float32) Option
```

Size sets the logical size of the window in pixels (default 800x600).

#### func StartHidden

```go
func StartHidden() Option
```

StartHidden opens the main window hidden (tela.App.Hidden): an app that starts in the tray. The fake window manager gives a hidden window no frames, so it draws nothing (no screenshot, no goldens, no actions that need a layout) until the app shows it; its components still build and its effects run (its tray icon shows, ADR-185).

#### func TextScale

```go
func TextScale(scale float64) Option
```

TextScale sets the system's text scale (default 1): 1rem is the theme's rem times scale, so text and rem-based spacing grow (tela.UseTextScale), unless the app sets tela.App.IgnoreTextScale. The scale is above 0 and at most 4.

#### func Theme

```go
func Theme(t tela.Theme) Option
```

Theme sets the app's theme, like tela.App.Theme: the color tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground), the base radius and the fonts. Without it the app has tela.DefaultTheme. tela.SetTheme changes it while the app runs.

#### func Timeout

```go
func Timeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

Timeout sets how long actions and expectations wait for their condition before they fail the test (default [`DefaultTimeout`](#constants)). It is wall-clock time, as in Playwright, while the app's clock moves one frame at a time during the wait. It also bounds, in app time (up to [`DefaultTimeout`](#constants)), how long a single action lets the app run before it stops waiting for it to go quiet (an animation that never ends is logged, not waited for); a finite animation runs to its end however slow the machine is.

#### func Title

```go
func Title(title string) Option
```

Title sets the title of the main window (tela.App.Title), which [`App.Title`](#func-app-title) and [`App.Window`](#func-app-window) read. The default is "telatest".

#### func TitleBar

```go
func TitleBar(colors tela.TitleBarColors) Option
```

TitleBar sets the title bar colors of the main window (tela.App.TitleBar). The fake window manager only records them: [`App.TitleBar`](#func-app-titlebar) reads them back.

#### func TitleBarControls

```go
func TitleBarControls(r tela.Rect) Option
```

TitleBarControls gives every TitleBarOverlay window of the app the rectangle that the OS's window buttons cover ([`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate).TitleBarControls), in logical window coordinates, as macOS's traffic lights do. [`App.SetTitleBarControls`](#func-app-settitlebarcontrols) changes one window's later.

#### func TitleBarOverlay

```go
func TitleBarOverlay() Option
```

TitleBarOverlay puts the main window's content under a transparent title bar with the OS's window buttons over it (tela.App.TitleBarOverlay). The fake window manager keeps no buttons there unless the test says where: without [`TitleBarControls`](#func-titlebarcontrols) or [`PlatformKeys`](#func-platformkeys)("darwin") the window behaves as a Frameless one on a platform that cannot do this (Linux, Windows): ClientSideDecorations, and an empty [`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate) TitleBarControls. With PlatformKeys("darwin") the buttons are [`MacTitleBarControls`](#variables).

#### func Transparent

```go
func Transparent() Option
```

Transparent opens the main window transparent and frameless (tela.App.Transparent with Frameless): the root has no background, so the screenshots and goldens keep the frame's alpha, transparent where the app paints nothing, and pointer actions over pixels whose alpha is under a quarter (platform.InputAlpha) go to what is below the window: the app gets nothing ([`App.TakesInput`](#func-app-takesinput)). [`tela.WindowState`](API-Reference-tela#type-windowstate).Transparent is true unless [`NoCompositing`](#func-nocompositing).

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, Widget{}, telatest.Transparent(), telatest.Size(360, 240))
app.Golden("widget.png") // a PNG with alpha: the card and its shadow
```

#### func WithUnsupported

```go
func WithUnsupported(services ...DesktopService) Option
```

WithUnsupported makes the headless desktop lack the given services from the start, as [`App.Unsupported`](#func-app-unsupported) does later: for components that look at the platform when they mount.

```go
app := telatest.Mount(t, Root, telatest.WithUnsupported(telatest.AppMenu))
```

### type PopupMenu

```go
type PopupMenu struct {
    // At is the menu's top-left corner in its window, logical pixels.
    At    tela.Point
    Items []MenuItem
}
```

PopupMenu is a native context menu the app shows (desktop.PopupMenu) and the test has not answered.

### type Registration

```go
type Registration struct {
    // Association is "notes:" for a scheme, ".note" for a file type.
    Association string
    // App is what was registered as the handler.
    App desktop.HandlerApp
    // Role is the role registered (desktop.Association.WithRole),
    // resolved: desktop.HandlerDefault reads as HandlerEditor for a file
    // type and HandlerViewer for a scheme.
    Role desktop.HandlerRole
    // Default: the app is the default handler.
    Default bool
}
```

Registration is a URL scheme or a file type the app registered (desktop.Register, MakeDefault), as the headless desktop recorded it.

### type State

```go
type State struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

State is one condition on an element that [`App.Expect`](#func-app-expect) checks: a toggle such as [`Checked`](#func-checked), a flag such as [`Disabled`](#func-disabled), its [`HasName`](#func-hasname) and [`HasValue`](#func-hasvalue), or a widget property the aria snapshot does not print: [`HasPopup`](#func-haspopup), [`ActiveDescendant`](#func-activedescendant) and [`Controls`](#func-controls) (which compare the element an ID reference points to with the one a Locator finds). They read the element's semantics node, so they test what assistive technologies are told, without matching strings of the aria snapshot.

#### func ActiveDescendant

```go
func ActiveDescendant(loc Locator) State
```

ActiveDescendant expects the element's aria-activedescendant to point to the element that loc locates (one element, strictness): the option a combobox or a list box keeps its virtual focus on while the keyboard focus stays on the input (h.AriaActiveDescendant sets it). Use [`NoActiveDescendant`](#func-noactivedescendant) for none. The aria snapshot does not print it.

```go
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("combobox", "Project"),
    telatest.ActiveDescendant(telatest.ByRole("option", "users-db")))
```

#### func Checked

```go
func Checked(checked bool) State
```

Checked expects the element to have aria-checked equal to checked (a checkbox, radio, switch or option; h.AriaChecked sets it). An element without the state, or with the mixed one, does not satisfy it.

#### func Controls

```go
func Controls(loc Locator) State
```

Controls expects the element's aria-controls to point to the element that loc locates (one element, strictness): the list box of a combobox or the panel of a tab (h.AriaControls sets it). The aria snapshot does not print it.

```go
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("combobox", "Project"), telatest.Controls(telatest.ByRole("listbox", "Project")))
```

#### func Current

```go
func Current(current string) State
```

Current expects the element's aria-current to be current: "page", "step", "location", "date", "time" or "true", or "false", which is also what an element without h.AriaCurrent has (the ARIA default). The aria snapshot does not print it (Playwright's does not either).

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("link", "Docs"))
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("link", "Docs"), telatest.Current("page"))
```

#### func Disabled

```go
func Disabled(disabled bool) State
```

Disabled expects the element to be disabled (true) or enabled (false): disabled by h.Disabled on it or an ancestor, or by h.AriaDisabled.

#### func Expanded

```go
func Expanded(expanded bool) State
```

Expanded expects the element to have aria-expanded equal to expanded (what a button, link or combobox controls; h.AriaExpanded sets it).

#### func Focused

```go
func Focused(focused bool) State
```

Focused expects the element to have the keyboard focus (true) or not (false).

#### func HasName

```go
func HasName(name string) State
```

HasName expects the element's accessible name to be exactly name (white space normalized, case sensitive): what [`ByRole`](#func-byrole) matches by.

#### func HasPopup

```go
func HasPopup(kind string) State
```

HasPopup expects the element's aria-haspopup to be kind: "menu", "listbox", "tree", "grid" or "dialog" (h.AriaHasPopup sets it), or "" for an element that opens no popup. As in ARIA, "true" is "menu" and "false" is "". The aria snapshot does not print it (Playwright's does not either).

```go
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("button", "Show suggestions"), telatest.HasPopup("listbox"))
```

#### func HasValue

```go
func HasValue(value string) State
```

HasValue expects the element's value to be exactly value: the text of a text field, or the value text of a range widget (the h.AriaValueText or h.AriaValueNow of a slider or progress bar, as in the aria snapshot).

#### func Invalid

```go
func Invalid(invalid bool) State
```

Invalid expects the element's value to be invalid (true) or valid (false) for assistive technologies: h.AriaInvalid when it is set, else a text field's own validity (an email or url Input whose value does not parse; a ReadOnly or disabled field is never invalid by its value), as Chromium tells them.

```go
app.Fill(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Email"), "ada@")
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Email"), telatest.Invalid(true))
```

#### func NoActiveDescendant

```go
func NoActiveDescendant() State
```

NoActiveDescendant expects the element to have no active descendant (no aria-activedescendant, or one whose element is not in the tree).

#### func Pressed

```go
func Pressed(pressed bool) State
```

Pressed expects the element to have aria-pressed equal to pressed (a toggle button; h.AriaPressed sets it).

#### func Selected

```go
func Selected(selected bool) State
```

Selected expects the element to have aria-selected equal to selected (a tab, option, row or cell; h.AriaSelected sets it).

#### func Sort

```go
func Sort(sort string) State
```

Sort expects the element's aria-sort to be sort: "ascending", "descending", "other" or "none", which is also what a header without h.AriaSort has (the ARIA default). The aria snapshot does not print it (Playwright's does not either).

```go
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("columnheader", "Name"))
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("columnheader", "Name"), telatest.Sort("descending"))
```

### type Stats

```go
type Stats = core.Stats
```

Stats counts the work of the app's tree since it was mounted: frames, component builds and skipped builds, style, layout and paint passes. A test uses the difference between two readings to assert how narrow an update was.

`Stats` is an alias of `core.Stats`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type Stats struct {
    Frames     int // Frame calls that ran the pipeline
    Builds     int // component builds
    Skips      int // component builds skipped (equal props, or the same node)
    Mounts     int // Elements mounted
    Unmounts   int // Elements unmounted
    Styles     int // style computations
    Structures int // box structure passes
    Shapes     int // paragraphs shaped (text.NewLayout)
    Breaks     int // paragraph line breakings (text.Layout.BreakLines)
    Layouts    int // layout passes (layout.Engine.Compute)
    Paints     int // paint passes
}
```

### type TextOption

```go
type TextOption func(*Locator)
```

TextOption configures [`ByText`](#func-bytext).

#### func Exact

```go
func Exact() TextOption
```

Exact makes [`ByText`](#func-bytext) match the whole text, case sensitive, instead of a case-insensitive substring.

### type TrayIcon

```go
type TrayIcon struct {
    Tooltip string
    Menu    []TrayItem
    // Updates counts the changes of the icon since it was added.
    Updates int
}
```

TrayIcon is a tray icon the app shows (a mounted desktop.Tray).

### type TrayItem

```go
type TrayItem struct {
    Label                        string
    Separator, Checkbox, Checked bool
    Disabled                     bool
    Submenu                      []TrayItem
}
```

TrayItem is an item of a tray icon's menu.

### type WindowCond

```go
type WindowCond struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

WindowCond is a condition on a window's state for [`App.ExpectWindowState`](#func-app-expectwindowstate).

#### func Active

```go
func Active(on bool) WindowCond
```

Active is met when the window is the active one, the one with the keyboard focus (WindowState.Focused), or is not.

#### func ClientDecorations

```go
func ClientDecorations(on bool) WindowCond
```

ClientDecorations is met when the app draws the window's title bar (WindowState.ClientSideDecorations: a Frameless window), or does not.

#### func Fullscreen

```go
func Fullscreen(on bool) WindowCond
```

Fullscreen is met when the window is (or is not) fullscreen.

#### func Hidden

```go
func Hidden(on bool) WindowCond
```

Hidden is met when the app has hidden the window (tela.Window.Hidden, WindowHandle.Hide), or has not.

#### func Maximized

```go
func Maximized(on bool) WindowCond
```

Maximized is met when the window is (or is not) maximized.

#### func Minimized

```go
func Minimized(on bool) WindowCond
```

Minimized is met when the window is (or is not) minimized.
